title: DynamicVis: Dynamic visual perception for efficient remote sensing foundation models
authors: Chen, KY; Liu, CY; Chen, BW; Li, WY; Zou, ZX; Lu, SJ; Shi, ZW
src: ISPRS JOURNAL OF PHOTOGRAMMETRY AND REMOTE SENSING
abstract: The continuous advancement of remote sensing technology has enabled high-resolution Earth observation; however, interpreting these expansive images using modern Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) remains a significant challenge. Unlike object-centric natural images, remote sensing imagery is fundamentally characterized by extreme target sparsity and massive spatial redundancy. Key objects of interest (e.g., ships, vehicles, scattered buildings) often occupy less than 1% of the spatial extent, surrounded by vast, target-free backgrounds. Many existing VFMs rely on uniform dense processing (e.g., Vision Transformers), while a substantial branch adopts pixel-reconstruction pre-training paradigms (e.g., Masked Autoencoders). These designs may waste substantial computational capacity on modeling redundant backgrounds and dilute the feature representations of small, sparse targets. To bridge this structural misalignment, we propose DynamicVis, a remote sensing visual foundation model explicitly tailored to spatial sparsity in high-resolution imagery, with a focus on largescale visual pre-training and transferable spatial representations for diverse downstream perception tasks. Architecturally, DynamicVis introduces a Dynamic Region-Aware State Space Model (SSM) that bypasses uniform computation. It adaptively routes and incrementally models only task-relevant, high-salience tokens while employing a parameter-free integration for background context, drastically reducing the complexity of processing ultra-long 2D token sequences (similar to 100,000). Crucially, to equip the network with robust spatial-selection capabilities, we propose a novel weakly supervised Region-Level Meta-Embedding Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) pre-training paradigm. Trained on a million-scale dataset, this paradigm promotes foreground-aware regional discrimination in the latent semantic space, mitigating the semantic ambiguity of conventional pixel-reconstruction methods. Extensive evaluations across nine diverse downstream visual perception tasks reveal that DynamicVis achieves competitive performance across region-, instance-, and pixel-level remote sensing tasks, with particularly strong results in sparse-target and instance-level perception tasks (e.g., small object detection and instance segmentation). Notably, DynamicVis processes high-resolution imagery (2048 & times; 2048) with merely 97 ms latency and 833 MB of memory consumption without employing any acceleration techniques (approximately 6% and 3% of a base ViT, respectively), offering a favorable trade-off between computational scalability and representation accuracy for multi-granular remote sensing analysis. Source code is available at https://github.com/KyanChen/DynamicVis.

title: TAM-YOLO: A Real-Time Detection Strategy for Small Objects Derived from Triaxial Attention Modeling
authors: Y. Xu; C. Dong
src: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering (ICBDSE)
abstract: Real-time object detection plays a pivotal role in multimedia big data analytics, where vast volumes of video and image data demand low-latency identification of objects. Yet, detecting small or easily occluded low-saliency targets within such complex data remains challenging. To address this, we propose TAM-YOLO, an improved YOLOv8-based detector tailored for robust object mining in multimedia data. First, to mitigate fine-grained information loss of small objects during downsampling, Spatial Group Convolution (SG-Conv) replaces strided convolution with space-to-depth rearrangement, preserving local details while reducing parameters. Second, to overcome the limited directional long-range dependency modeling of conventional attention, a Triaxial Attention Module (TAM) independently encodes attention along the horizontal, vertical, and channel dimensions, enhancing contour perception and channel discriminability. These improvements substantially strengthen feature representation and localization for small objects in data-intensive scenarios. Experiments on MS COCO 2017 and PASCAL VOC demonstrate that TAM-YOLO achieves competitive accuracy against the baseline and mainstream real-time detectors, offering an efficient solution for object detection in large-scale multimedia analysis.

title: Prompt-Driven Small Object Instance Segmentation in Earth Observation
authors: C. Wang; Y. Ji; Y. Meng; Y. Zhang; Y. Zhu
src: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
abstract: Extracting small objects from remote sensing imagery is essential for applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, and disaster management. While current research primarily targets small object detection, instance segmentation for small objects remains underexplored, largely due to the high cost and difficulty of obtaining pixel-level annotations. Recent progress in prompt-based segmentation, exemplified by the Segment Anything Model (SAM), enables large-scale and efficient mask generation. However, SAM's performance on small objects degrades significantly because its coarse feature resolution fails to capture fine spatial details. To address this issue, we propose SOPSeg, an adaptation of SAM tailored for prompted small-object segmentation in remote sensing imagery. SOPSeg introduces a region-adaptive magnification strategy to preserve local details, an edge-aware decoder with progressive refinement for precise boundaries, and an oriented prompting mechanism compatible with rotated bounding boxes commonly used in aerial imagery. SOPSeg outperforms existing prompt-based segmentation methods on three datasets and also enables efficient dataset construction for remote sensing tasks. Building on this capability, we further use SOPSeg to construct ReSOS, a large-scale small-object instance segmentation dataset automatically generated from SODA-A oriented bounding box annotations and refined through manual filtering. Both the framework and dataset will be publicly released to facilitate future research. Our source code can be found here.

title: Remote Sensing-Oriented Small-Object Detection Based on Rotation-Normalized Prompting Segment Anything Model
authors: B. Chai; J. Wang; Z. Zheng; L. Chen; X. Gong; W. Liu
src: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
abstract: Remote sensing object detection is critical for Earth observation and analysis. However, accurately detecting small objects remains a significant challenge due to complex and heterogeneous backgrounds as well as the inherently limited information these objects provide. While numerous specialized algorithms have been proposed to enhance small-object detection, the weak feature representation of objects within cluttered scenes continues to severely limit performance, making this a persistent and open research problem. Therefore, in this article, to enhance the discriminative representation of small objects in a complex background, a novel two-phase rotation-normalized prompting-oriented small-object detection (RNP-OSOD) framework is proposed. In the first mask generation phase, a rotation-normalized prompt for segment anything model (RNP-SAM) is proposed to obtain high-quality instance and semantic mask annotations. In this method, image patches containing objects are cropped, enlarged, and rotation-normalized to acquire RNP before being fed into SAM, which then produces accurate mask supervision for training. In the second mask supervising object detection phase, to amplify the feature responses of small objects and balance instances across different scales, a scale-adaptive instance focusing (SAIF) loss is proposed by employing the generated masks as supervisory signals. This loss comprises an area-guided semantic reconstruction loss, called scale-adaptive semantic (SAS) loss and a detection-decoupled instance segmentation loss. To rigorously evaluate the proposed framework, we conduct extensive experiments on the small object detection datasets (SODAs) and create a new dataset, Small-DOTA, constructed by filtering and downsampling DOTA to match SODA’s characteristics. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across both benchmarks. The source code will be available at https://github.com/cbq233333/RNP-OSOD

title: AF-YOLO: A High-Precision Aircraft Safety Wire Segmentation Network for Assembly Quality Inspection
authors: R. Yang; X. Zhang
src: 2026 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electronic Technology, Communication and Information (ICETCI)
abstract: The assurance of aircraft assembly quality is a fundamental prerequisite for flight safety, and safety wires, serving as critical locking mechanisms for fasteners, play a decisive role in preventing mechanical loosening and structural instability caused by in-flight vibrations, where a missing or improperly installed wire can lead to catastrophic risks. However, the automated detection and segmentation of these wires pose significant challenges for computer vision algorithms due to their extremely slender geometric shapes, metallic reflection, and dense arrangement within complex mechanical backgrounds. Existing real-time instance segmentation models, such as YOLOv8-seg, often suffer from feature noise when processing such strip-like objects and lose fine-grained details during deep downsampling operations. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved network, AF-YOLO (Aircraft Fuse/Safety-wire YOLO), which first introduces an Asymmetric Convolution Block (ACB) to replace standard square convolutions in the backbone, decomposing spatial extraction into horizontal (1×3) and vertical (3×1) directions to enhance the model's sensitivity to the slender shape of fuses while reducing background redundancy, and further leverages structural re-parameterization to merge these branches during inference with no additional latency. In addition, a P2 Micro-Scale Prediction Head is constructed on a high-resolution feature map (4× downsampling) to recover texture information of tiny fuses typically lost in deeper layers. Extensive experimental results on a custom aircraft fuse dataset demonstrate that AFYOLO achieves a mask mAP@0.5 of 87.2%, outperforming the baseline YOLOv8-seg by 2.7%, and specifically improves the detection of small objects $(A P_{S})$ by 4.5%, thereby balancing accuracy and speed and making the method suitable for intelligent aviation assembly tasks.

title: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Dynamic Query Embedding for Instance Segmentation
authors: X. Xu
src: 2026 5th International Symposium on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Information Engineering (RAIIE)
abstract: Instance segmentation is a core computer vision task that classifies individual objects and segments their pixel regions, with wide applications in autonomous driving, intelligent surveillance, and medical image analysis. However, existing methods suffer from insufficient small-object feature capture, rigid feature fusion, and non-adaptive query numbers, severely limiting their accuracy and robustness in complex scenes. To address these issues, this paper proposes an instance segmentation algorithm based on multi-scale feature fusion and dynamic query embedding. A dual-path feature enhancement and fusion module is introduced to preserve local structural and global semantic features via channel-wise calibration and spatial-wise interaction, improving scale adaptability and small-object capture. A Transformer decoder with instance-aware dynamic query embedding dynamically adjusts query number and distribution based on scene complexity, enhancing generalization. On the OCID dataset, experimental results show that our method achieves the superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Learnable Sliced Wasserstein Barycenter for Knowledge Distillation in Autonomous Driving
authors: H. Lu; M. Zhang; Z. Liu; H. Jing
abstract: In the field of end-to-end autonomous driving, deep learning-based vision models have demonstrated remarkable effectiveness, especially when confronted with challenging scenarios featuring numerous dynamic objects. However, they also come with excessive energy consumption and significant power constraints. Knowledge Distillation provides a cost-efficient methodology for transferring expert knowledge from comprehensive models to compact models. However, extracting and migrating high-quality knowledge representations for knowledge distillation remains a challenging task demanding significant effort. Our methodology involves a precise computation of the Learnable Sliced Wasserstein Barycenter (Learnable SWB), a metric that captures the centrality measure between the output distributions of the comprehensive model and the encoder distribution of Ground Truth crafted by a Label Mapping. To streamline the knowledge transfer process while ensuring the retention of crucial information, we propose Batch-Aware SWD and Instance-Aware SWD. In contrast to directly fitting the output distributions of the compact model to the barycenter, we treat the output distribution of student model as a learnable centrality measure. By optimizing the Batch-Aware SWD and Instance-Aware SWD, we achieve efficient knowledge transfer with key information preserved. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our methodology in object detection and instance segmentation for autonomous driving, achieving significant improvements in the accuracy of autonomous driving datasets.

title: Improved YOLOv11n-based Instance Segmentation for Tiny Objects in UAV Imagery
authors: Z. Zhao; T. Wu; J. Zhang; Y. Dong
src: 2026 7th International Conference on Computer Vision, Image and Deep Learning (CVIDL)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of targets within Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery remains a formidable challenge, primarily because objects are often diminutive and embedded in chaotic backgrounds. To surmount these obstacles, we present an enhanced instance segmentation architecture built upon the YOLOv11n framework. Our methodology introduces three strategic modifications: first, we integrate the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to sharpen the model's focus on salient features; second, we deploy the DySample operator to replace standard upsampling, thereby better safeguarding fine-grained details during reconstruction; and third, a specialized P2 detection head is appended explicitly to capture micro-scale targets. Empirical analysis reveals that while DySample offers limited utility in isolation, it functions synergistically with CBAM to yield substantial performance gains. Furthermore, although the P2 head incurs a higher training loss, it provides a critical boost to detection precision. Benchmarks on the VisDrone2019 dataset confirm the validity of our approach, registering improvements of 1.0% in Mask mAP@0.5 and 0.29% in Mask mAP@0.5:0.95 over the baseline YOLOv11n model.

title: SCM-YOLO: A Spatial-Channel-Multi-Scale Collaborative Framework for Litchi Instance Segmentation in Complex Orchard Environments
authors: Y. Xue; J. Zhang; H. Liu; H. Xiao; B. Chen; Y. Wu
src: 2026 11th International Conference on Electronic Technology and Information Science (ICETIS)
abstract: Instance segmentation of litchi fruits in complex orchard environments is challenging due to small object size, dense distribution, occlusion, and illumination interference. To address these issues, this paper proposes SCM-YOLO, a spatialchannel-multi-scale collaborative enhancement framework based on YOLOv9-Seg. Instead of directly stacking attention mechanisms, the proposed method integrates SimAM for spatial feature enhancement, ECA for channel-wise feature recalibration, and BiFPN for multi-scale feature fusion. These modules are collaboratively embedded into different stages of the network to improve feature representation under complex conditions. A UAV-based litchi dataset containing 1,468 images and 25,520 annotated instances is constructed for evaluation, and an additional public apple instance segmentation dataset is introduced to examine the generalization behavior of the proposed framework on another fruit category. Experimental results show that SCM-YOLO achieves 0.8683 mAP50-Box and 0.8621 mAP50-Mask, outperforming YOLOv9-Seg by 6.57% and 5.33%, respectively. Ablation studies further demonstrate that the collaborative integration of spatial, channel, and multi-scale features leads to consistent performance improvements. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for intelligent orchard management and can be extended to other agricultural instance segmentation tasks.

title: TEA-YOLO-seg: A Lightweight Instance Segmentation Algorithm for Tender Tea Leaf
authors: W. Bi; L. Yu; W. Xu; X. Yin
abstract: Instance segmentation of tender tea leaf is an important prerequisite for conducting tea yield estimation. However, existing You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based segmentation methods face challenges in achieving high accuracy, particularly in recognizing small tender tea leaf within complex environments. To address this limitation, we propose TEA-YOLO-seg, a modified algorithm based on YOLOv11n-seg, which enhances small target detection and segmentation performance. First, an improved PP-LCNet is adopted as the backbone to lower computational cost while enhancing small-target feature extraction. Second, an optimized SimAM attention mechanism is integrated to strengthen feature representation in small-target regions. Finally, the normalized Wasserstein distance (NWD) loss is incorporated, which applies a scale penalty and small-target weighting mechanism to mitigate scale imbalance. Experiments on a self-constructed tea garden dataset show that TEAYOLO-seg outperforms the original model, reducing parameters by 0.46 M and improving precision by 9.36%, recall by 12.63%, and mean average precision (mAP)@0.5 and mAP@0.5–0.95 by 11.27% and 6.95%, respectively. Moreover, it also outperforms the YOLOv5-10n-seg model. Thus, the proposed method can provide robust support for tea yield estimation in tea garden management.

title: MEF-Net: Mamba-Based Multidomain Edge Feature Fusion Network for City Infrastructure Detection in Remote Sensing Images
authors: P. Sun; L. Yang; L. Liang; H. Yang; D. Liu; X. Li
src: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
abstract: Timely detection of urban infrastructure is crucial for city planning, routine maintenance, and disaster response. Remote sensing imagery provides large-scale coverage, enabling monitoring of key facilities, such as buildings. However, arbitrary orientations, dense distributions, small sizes, and blurred boundaries of targets in remote sensing images pose significant challenges to accurate detection. To address these issues, we propose a multidomain edge feature fusion network (MEF-Net), which integrates Mamba and attention-guided receptive field mechanisms to enhance edge perception and multiscale feature fusion. Specifically, the Mamba-based multiscale edge fusion and selection block fuses multi-domain feature information, including spatial, frequency, channel, and multiscale features, and utilizes Mamba to effectively fuse critical cues, alleviating issues related to boundary ambiguity and scale variation. The attention-guided receptive field interchange block adaptively enlarges the receptive field through attention mechanisms, incorporating spatial and channel information to improve the perception of small and oriented targets. The Gated Mamba Shuffle Fusion employs Mamba with a gated mechanism to suppress irrelevant regions and enhance feature selection and fusion. The receptive field expansion-based adaptive multitask detection head (RFE-AMD) improves global feature capture while preserving local details via adaptive gated decomposition and group normalization. RFE-AMD supports horizontal and rotated object detection, and instance segmentation for comprehensive infrastructure analysis. Extensive experiments are conducted on four public datasets, compared to 46 detection and instance segmentation models. The results show that MEF-Net achieves state-of-the-art mean Average Precision across all tasks, demonstrating superior performance in complex remote sensing scenarios while balancing parameters and inference speed.

title: Class Difficulty-Aware Real-Time Instance Segmentation
authors: Y. Zhao; L. Zhou; H. Zhang; F. Tong; Z. Hu
src: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Existing transformer-based real-time instance segmentation methods often exhibit bias toward salient regions while performing poorly on small objects. We identify small objects as inherently difficult classes and attribute this limitation to the imbalanced query difficulty distribution in transformer-based approaches. We first introduce the class difficulty to characterize the dynamic evolution of class-learning degree during training and we propose Class Difficulty Awareness (CDA) module to dynamically quantify class difficulty. Based on CDA, a Difficulty-Class Enhanced Query is proposed to balance the difficulty distribution of queries through oversampling difficult class queries, and a re-weighting loss is proposed to adaptively adjust the importance of difficult class, to improve difficult class segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on COCO and Cityscapes demonstrate that our approach establishing new accuracy-speed trade-off. Notably, on COCO with R50-d-DCN backbone, our method attains 41.5% AP, surpassing prior SOTA by 1.1% AP and 5.9% APs improvement, while maintaining real-time inference speed.

title: Comparison Study of One-Stage and Two-Stage Instance Segmentation Methods in Different Application Scenarios
authors: X. Li
src: 2026 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Algorithms (CAIBDA)
abstract: Instance segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that simultaneously provides object categories, bounding boxes, and pixel-level masks. Existing methods can be broadly categorized into two paradigms: two-stage approaches, such as Mask R-CNN, which prioritize accuracy through a coarse-to-fine pipeline, and one-stage approaches, such as YOLACT, SOLOv2, and YOLOv8-seg, which emphasize inference efficiency through end-to-end dense prediction. However, systematic discussions of how these paradigms differ across practical application scenarios remain insufficient. To address this issue, this paper organizes a scenario-oriented comparative study of four representative instance segmentation models based on public benchmark results and reported implementation settings on COCO 2017 and Cityscapes. The comparison is conducted under common evaluation dimensions, including segmentation accuracy, inference efficiency, and computational complexity, rather than as a fully controlled re-implementation benchmark. The summarized results suggest that Mask R-CNN maintains an advantage in small-object segmentation due to its region proposal and feature alignment mechanisms, while SOLOv2 achieves strong overall mask accuracy and high-IoU performance among the compared models. In contrast, YOLOv8-seg shows a prominent inference-speed advantage under the reported settings while retaining competitive segmentation quality, indicating potential for latency-sensitive applications such as autonomous driving and real-time monitoring. These observations show that model selection should not be determined solely by the one-stage or two-stage paradigm, but should instead consider the specific requirements of the target scenario, including segmentation precision, object scale, inference latency, and computational resources. Based on these findings, this paper provides practical, scenario-driven guidelines for selecting instance segmentation models under different accuracy, speed, and resource constraints.

title: YOLO-ITC: A New YOLO Method for Instance Segmentation of Individual Tree Crowns
authors: Z. Sun; B. Xue; M. Zhang; J. Schindler
src: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence
abstract: The instance segmentation task of individual tree crowns is an important real-world application that facilitates forest management, carbon storage estimation, and biodiversity modelling. Recently, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved great success in computer vision. Several efforts have applied CNNs to perform instance segmentation of tree canopies. However, the existing CNN works rarely consider instance segmentation and species classification of densely distributed small and medium tree crowns. YOLO, as a fast and effective method, shows promising results in the field of instance segmentation and canopy detection and segmentation. We utilize a tree crown dataset from Wellington, Aotearoa, New Zealand, based on aerial imagery which contains small and medium-sized tree objects distributed across a diverse rural landscape ranging from isolated trees to dense forest stands. We propose a new YOLO method for individual tree crowns (ITC) based on YOLOv7, named YOLO-ITC. Specifically, a new detection design targeting small and medium trees is first proposed. Based on this, we propose a Dense Block module for the main block of the backbone in a densely connected way, where the previous features are reused to aggregate more useful information. Finally, efficient attention is embedded in the Dense Block to capture the globally long-range dependencies. Extensive experimental results show that the proposed method, YOLO-ITC, achieves both higher detection and mask accuracy over other commonly used baseline models.

title: Platform Selection, Sensor Trade-Offs, and Architecture Performance: A Decision Framework for Operational Wildlife Monitoring
authors: L. A. Gonzalez-Guevara; D. Celeita; A. Cardenas; J. R. Montoya-Torres
abstract: Fragile Andean moorlands lack of pipeline methodologies for aerial wildlife monitoring. This situation enables invasive anthropocentric pressures, which negatively impact the ecosystem. Operational deployment of cattle monitoring requires navigating through critical trade-offs among pipeline decisions into the system design. This comprehensive review synthesizes relevant studies in the last decade, following PRISMA methodology, from platform capabilities to architectural trade-offs focused in their application to moorland ecosystems in order to establish operational computer vision pipelines. Aerial platform characteristics determine spatial resolution as well as pre-processing and architectural needs. UAVs cover medium scales with trade-off in ground sampling distance. This spatial resolution makes them optimal for surveys under 50 km2. Manned aircraft and VHR satellites become cost-effective only beyond 100 km2, but resolution degrades. Sensor decision depends on habitat type characteristics. Sensor fusion quantification demonstrates that thermal-RGB integration improves species detection, in order to justify cost in heterogeneous habitats versus RGB sufficient for open landscapes that achieves higher precision. Pre-processing impact assessment shows ESRGAN super-resolution provides detection gain for objects at altitudes up 250 meters, whereas CLAHE enhancement deliver high classification accuracy at negligible computational cost. Architecture performance taxonomy establishes YOLO variants dominate real-time embedded systems, transformer models justify computational overhead exclusively in multi-species scenarios, and density regression achieves MAE below 10 for ultra-dense aggregations. Critical deployment barriers include performance degradation across altitude variations, domain generalization failures that require annotation effort reduction through point-based weak supervision, and absence in transfer learning protocols for data-sparse ecosystems. This review establishes methodological foundations for high-altitude Andean moorland conservation where operational datasets remain absent, in order to provide quantitative decision matrices applicable to fragile mountainous ecosystems globally that requires evidence-based monitoring system design.

title: Benchmarking YOLO Models in Detecting Small On-Tree Immature Peaches for Precision Thinning
authors: A. Andreadis; I. Kostelidis; T. Kalampokas; E. Vrochidou; G. A. Papakostas
src: 2026 International Congress on Smart Agriculture and Sustainable Systems Engineering (SmartAgri&SuSY)
abstract: Peach tree cluster thinning is an essential practice for removing excess fruit from branches to promote larger, higher-quality fruit, prevent branch damage, and maintain better long-term tree health. Shortage of a seasoned workforce to manually thin peach trees, as well as related ever increasing management costs, triggered the development of computer vision algorithms towards automating processes. In this context, this work proposes an original public real-world on-tree peach image dataset including 5,597 images of 77,427 instances, captured at the appropriate timing for thinning, in early spring, introducing challenges such as small, overlapping fruit, not easily distinguished within dense green foliage. Four medium-sized You Only Look Once (YOLO) family models are comparatively evaluated for peach fruit detection in such a complex orchard environment, aiming to highlight the best fit for the problem under study. Results indicate the overall efficiency of YOLO family models to support peach fruit detection towards developing artificial intelligence (AI)-based cluster thinning precision agriculture systems. Among the examined models, YOLOv11 offers the best trade-off between the model’s complexity, task performance and computational requirements, making it well-suited for use in real-world orchard applications.

title: ARANet: A Unified Representation Alignment Framework for SAR Ship Instance Segmentation
authors: S. Chang; P. Lang; H. Chang; C. Zhao; J. Yang; J. Dong; X. Fu
src: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
abstract: Deep learning has become the dominant paradigm for ship instance segmentation in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image. However, reliable segmentation in complex maritime environments remains constrained by three representational misalignments: inconsistency between semantic and structural cues, imbalance in global-local contextual modeling, and limited adaptability to cross-dataset scale variations. To address these challenges, we propose the adaptive representation alignment network (ARANet), a unified representation alignment framework that systematically reconciles these misalignments through three complementary alignment mechanisms. Specifically, ARANet enhances semantic-structural consistency via an edge-guided boundary refinement mechanism, balances global and local contextual representations through a context-aware modeling mechanism, and improves scale adaptability using a depth-adaptive feature alignment mechanism. These mechanisms are instantiated as the edge-guided boundary refinement module, the context-aware module, and the depth-adaptive feature pyramid network, respectively, and are integrated into a unified end-to-end architecture. Extensive experiments on the HRSID and PSeg-SAR Ship Detection Dataset datasets demonstrate that ARANet achieves leading or competitive performance compared with convolutional neural network-based, transformer-based, and SAR-specific instance segmentation methods.

title: Panoptic Segmentation for Intelligent Fishing Port Environment Recognition Using Mask2Former
authors: Liu Y.-M.; Hsieh Y.-Z.
src: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Consumer Technology, ICCT-Pacific 2026
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent technologies, automation in fishing port operations has become an important direction toward realizing smart fisheries. However, the fishing port environment is highly complex and dynamic, posing challenges to the perception and navigation capabilities of Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGVs). To address this issue, this study proposes a Mask2Former-based fishing port environment recognition system that integrates semantic and instance segmentation tasks through panoptic segmentation, enabling effective identification of various 'thing' and 'stuff' objects in fishing ports, such as personnel, baskets, and roads. The system is trained on a self-collected fishing port image dataset and compared with methods such as Panoptic-FPN and MaskFormer. Experimental results show that Mask2Former performs excellently in metrics including Panoptic Quality (PQ), Segmentation Quality (SQ), and Recognition Quality (RQ), particularly demonstrating advantages in recognizing small objects and handling complex backgrounds. Although its inference speed is slightly slower, it provides more precise segmentation results, making it highly promising for automation applications requiring high accuracy.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Automatic Vertebral Body Segmentation Performance in Lateral Thoracic Spine X-Rays: A Comparative Analysis Based on Implant Presence and Subtype
authors: Park J.K.; Baik Y.S.; Kim Y.J.; Yee G.-T.; Kim K.G.
src: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
abstract: Accurate vertebral body segmentation in spine radiographs is essential for quantitative analysis, but metallic implants introduce artifacts that degrade model performance. We evaluated the effects of implant presence and material subtypes on automatic segmentation using real-world thoracic spine lateral X-rays. SOLOv2 and Mask R-CNN were evaluated on radiographs from 264 patients. To analyze the localized impact of surgical hardware, a synchronized cohort of 3637 vertebral bodies correctly delineated by both models was analyzed, comparing non-implanted (n = 3467) and implanted (n = 170) instances. The implanted group was stratified into four subtypes: Bone Cement, Screw, Screw + Cement, and Screw + Etc. Performance was quantified via precision, sensitivity, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff distance (HD95), and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD), and validated using the Mann–Whitney U test (α = 0.010). Implant presence caused significant performance degradation across all metrics (p < 0.001). The Screw + Etc subgroup showed the most profound degradation versus baseline (DSC: 0.826 vs. 0.930, p < 0.001). The Screw subgroup exhibited significant declines in volumetric overlap and boundary distances (p < 0.010). The Bone Cement subgroup showed a broad multidimensional decline, including a severe drop in sensitivity (p < 0.001), while the Screw + Cement subgroup demonstrated significant distance-based errors (p = 0.005). Implant presence significantly reduces thoracic spine segmentation performance, varying distinctly by subtype. Developers must account for these subtype-specific artifacts to ensure clinical validity. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine 2026.

title: Domain-adaptive instance segmentation for far-field object monitoring using SAM-based weak supervision and noisy student self-training
authors: Koo M.; Kim T.; Lee M.; Kim K.; Kim H.
abstract: Automating construction site monitoring through deep learning–based segmentation presents challenges due to the high cost of pixel-wise annotations. This paper introduces a weakly and self-supervised learning framework that enhances segmentation accuracy while reducing annotation burden. Human-annotated bounding-box ground truth is used as prompts for the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate high-quality polygon mask labels, which are further refined through self-training. Compared to fully supervised learning models, the framework integrates Transfer Learning, Pseudo-Label Refinement, and the Noisy Student technique, improving mask mean Average Precision (Mask mAP) by 3–63% across seven target domains and achieving a Mask mAP of 72.27%. The approach also outperforms existing weakly supervised techniques, including BoxSnake and BoxTeacher, by 18% and 25.95%, respectively, and exceeds the performance of point-based methods such as PointWSSIS by 48.78%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Segment-based UAV Tracking via Shape-Aware Kalman Filter
authors: Jun Y.W.; Kim S.-C.
src: KSII Transactions on Internet and Information Systems
abstract: This study proposes a segmentation-based framework for real-time unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) tracking in complex visual environments. Conventional tracking approaches rely on bounding boxes and centroid-based Kalman filters, which are typically ineffective under occlusion, small object scale, and nonlinear UAV motion. In contrast, the proposed method uses pixel-wise segmentation masks to achieve precise object localization and integrates a shape-aware Kalman filter that models both the motion and geometric properties of UAVs. The state vector is extended to include the area, aspect ratio, and orientation, thereby enabling robust identity preservation during rapid movement and partial visibility. Fast-SCNN is used as a lightweight segmentation backbone to balance real-time inference and spatial accuracy. We benchmark the proposed framework on the Anti-UAV dataset, demonstrating significant reductions in identity switches by up to 84% while maintaining competitive overall tracking performance (multiple object tracking accuracy (MOTA) improvement of 3.7%) compared to state-of-the-art detection-based trackers (YOLOv3, Faster R-CNN, and Tracktor). The proposed framework has strong potential for UAV monitoring applications requiring fine-grained object representation, stable identity tracking, and computational efficiency in real-world scenarios. ⓒ 2026 KSII.

title: Combining RGB imaging with a two-stage deep learning method to reveal genetic variation of wheat sprouting traits
authors: Qin B.; Zhu X.; Deng H.; Liu X.; Wu Q.; Zhou H.; Fan S.; Min H.; Liang S.; Sang W.; Huang M.; Chen J.; Gao C.; Tu J.; Zhai S.; Hu X.; Liu M.; Zhou Y.; Jiang D.; Zhang Z.; Li Q.
abstract: Wheat emergence rate and emergence uniformity are key indicators for evaluating seed vigor and sowing quality, and they play an important role in wheat growth and yield formation. Traditional methods for measuring emergence rate and evaluating emergence uniformity rely on manual assessment, which is inefficient, highly subjective, and unable to meet the demand for large scale, high efficiency, and precise acquisition of wheat emergence data. In this study, RGB images and a two-stage deep learning algorithm were used to extract and analyze seedling traits of 420 wheat varieties under two nitrogen levels, and the results were applied to genome wide association studies to elucidate the genetic basis. The two-stage algorithm integrates a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network, small object detection layer, large size image input, and FasterNet to improve detection and instance segmentation speed and accuracy. The proposed method achieved an emergence rate accuracy of 0.929, with R2 = 0.914 and RMSE = 2.448 compared to manual measurements, and required less than 0.2 s per image for analysis. By employing this two-stage algorithm for processing and analysis, varieties (e.g., Gao8901 and ShiYou20) that consistently exhibited high emergence rates and uniformity under multiple nitrogen treatments were identified. Furthermore, genome-wide association study identified the major loci qEmergence rate-3A and qUniformity-6B governing seedling emergence rate and uniformity, which likely enhance wheat seedling traits by modulating energy supply or related signaling molecules. The emergence-rate and uniformity data generated by the two-stage algorithm significantly accelerated the discovery of relevant genes and enabled the identification of wheat varieties with high emergence rate and uniformity, providing valuable insights and practical references for high-quality breeding and gene mining. © 2026 The Authors. title: An Optimized Leakage-Aware YOLO-Based Deep Learning Framework for Instance Segmentation and Environmental Impact Assessment of Mixed Metal and Glass Waste
authors: Shafik A.N.; Khafagy M.H.; Aziz A.S.; Hussein S.A.
abstract: Accurate instance segmentation of recyclable waste is important for automated sorting and circular economy applications. Mixed metal and glass municipal waste is challenging because metal surfaces are often reflective, while glass objects have transparent boundaries and high visual variability. This paper presents a controlled computer vision framework that uses instance segmentation as an object-level perception layer for mixed metal and glass waste and links eligible detections to screening-level WARM-based environmental interpretation. A seven-class annotated dataset of 1667 images was evaluated using a fixed train/validation/test split. Model development used the validation split for architecture screening, optimization tuning, transfer learning analysis, seed selection, and NMS selection, and the held-out test set was used only for final evaluation. Using mask mAP@50:95 as the primary segmentation metric, the selected YOLOv8m-seg model achieved 0.9435 on the locked test set and obtained a higher mask mAP@50:95 than Mask R-CNN and RF-DETR-Seg under the same locked test protocol. Image-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were also used to characterize uncertainty around the locked test segmentation comparison. For environmental reporting, mass-bearing detections were mapped to class-specific mass priors and EPA WARM v16 factors rather than direct mask area-to-mass conversion; the masks were used for instance-level separation, localization, and visual verification, not as direct physical mass measurements. Under the stated assumptions, the framework produced screening-level environmental estimates of 1113.57 MJ of energy savings and 70.20 kg CO2e of avoided emissions, decreasing to 445.67 MJ and 28.62 kg CO2e after applying recycling rate priors. Overall, the framework provides a leakage-aware workflow linking instance segmentation to material-specific WARM-based environmental screening. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Accurate Segmentation of Overlapping Cervical Cells Using an Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Cytology Screening
authors: Alzu’bi A.A.; Khatatbeh M.; Mustafa W.A.; Zain N.M.; Alquran H.; Al-Mohtaseb A.; Alawneh K.Z.; Fawaeer M.; Fawaeer B.; Salameh S.; Alhussain A.
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity among women worldwide. The Papanicolaou (Pap) smear is widely used for early detection; however, its manual interpretation is time-consuming, requires substantial expertise, and is often affected by inter-observer variability, particularly in cases with dense and overlapping cells. Methods: This study developed an optimized deep learning framework for cervical cell instance segmentation, specifically targeting the separation of overlapping cells in Pap smear images. The proposed framework was based on Mask R-CNN with a ResNet-50 backbone and Feature Pyramid Network. A public development dataset of 460 cervical smear images was used for model development and internal evaluation, while an independent 210-image dataset collected from King Abdullah University Hospital was reserved as an external held-out clinical assessment set. To improve small-cell detection and mask refinement, the Region Proposal Network was adapted using biologically informed anchor scales (16, 32, 64, 128, 256), followed by soft calibration-based post-processing. Results: The proposed framework achieved an AP50 of 89.90% and a Mask IoU of 90.44%. Small-cell performance, measured using APs under the COCO small-object convention, reached 22.80%, while APm and APl reached 68.45% and 81.42%, respectively. Clinical cell-count evaluation on the independent KAUH held-out set was performed using the mean count of five physicians as the reference standard and achieved an overall clinical detection accuracy of 93.00%. Conclusions: The optimized Mask R-CNN framework improved the detection and separation of overlapping cervical cells in Pap smear images and may serve as a supportive tool for cytopathology workflows. The results suggest that biologically informed anchor optimization and soft calibration can improve cell-level instance segmentation, particularly for small and overlapping cells. Further validation on larger multi-center datasets remains necessary before routine clinical deployment. © 2026 by the authors.

title: A Hybrid Approach for Efficient and Precise Food Detection Using YOLOv9 and RCNN
authors: Keshari S.K.; Yadav A.; Shukla A.; Garg N.; Kumar V.
abstract: Identifying food items on plates is difficult. There is a wide variety of foods. Each food item can be complex. Because different backgrounds on the plates also create difficulties. Additionally, food items can be occluded by other objects. These factors make detection more complex. In this paper, a hybrid model is proposed to overcome such problems. The hybridization of two state-of-the-art deep learning models: Mask R-CNN and YOLOv9 are used for food detection on plates. These models are evaluated against a broad set of plate images based on metrics including mean average precision (mAP), precision, recall and inference speed. The result shows the significant improvement that the hybrid model performs better, with a score of 91.57% mAP and a 90.17% F1 score. The result is better than other state of art which successfully balancing speed and accuracy in detection and segmentation in complex scenarios. After analyzing the proposed model the potential suggestions for future directions are suggested, such as handling occlusions and increasing robustness for small objects. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: A comprehensive review of deep learning methods for weed classification in precision agriculture
authors: Ekene N.C.; Okoye F.A.; Chidi E.U.; Nnenna O.M.
abstract: Weeds today are among the factors contributing to low agricultural productivity. As the world’s population continues to grow, there is an urgent need to meet global food demand. Nigeria currently lacks sufficient crop production to feed its growing population, and weeds are among the core contributors to poor agricultural yield. This study conducts a comprehensive review of Deep Learning (DL) approaches to weed classification in precision agriculture, covering literature from 2018 to 2025, was carried out. We employed a mix of quantitative and qualitative methods in the course of this review paper. Our data source is centred on Scopus-indexed papers, published with Sensors, Electronics, and Agriculture in MDPI as well as IEEE, Thomson Reuters, and Springer. The study systematically reviewed and analysed machine learning (ML), DL, and instance segmentation techniques to identify the key technological and environmental barriers, such as data limitations, class imbalance, environmental variability, and model scalability issues that affect the effectiveness and efficiency of these models when deployed in real time. These findings show that while weed management models like the YOLO variants, ResNet, and Vision Transformers achieved high accuracy in training and testing, they are associated with several challenges in their real world-deployment, such as occlusion, small object detection, and environmental adaptability. Overall, this research provides recommended solutions to enhance model robustness, scalability, and efficiency. It further provides a summary of the current state and future directions for AI-driven weed management. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Shoreline-Adaptive Plastic Segmentation Network (SAPS-Net): A Dual-Cascade Framework with Cross-Modulated Feature Fusion for Automated Coastal Litter Monitoring
authors: Chen J.; Wen Z.; Zhou C.; Xu M.; Yang M.
abstract: Automated monitoring of coastal plastic pollution is critical for environmental management, but is severely hindered by the complexity of shoreline environments. Generic computer vision models fail due to extreme scale variation (from large nets to small fragments), complex background clutter (e.g., seaweed, rocks), and object deformation. We introduce the Shoreline-Adaptive Plastic Segmentation Network (SAPS-Net), a novel dual-cascade framework that addresses these “in-the-wild” challenges. SAPS-Net first classifies the shoreline’s environmental context (e.g., sandy, rocky) to dynamically load a specialized “expert” segmentation model. The model integrates bespoke modules for scale-adaptive attention and noise-gated dynamic convolution to precisely segment both large debris and small fragments. Trained on our new, large-scale Coastal Plastic Litter Data set (CPLD), SAPS-Net achieves a state-of-the-art 70.1% Average Precision (AP), significantly outperforming baselines (e.g., +17.6 AP vs Mask R-CNN). Crucially, it demonstrates a 10.0-point improvement in small-object AP (APs), addressing the most prevalent form of pollution. Empirical validation in a real-world field study (Hebei Province) confirmed the model’s robustness, achieving 0.90 F1-score and 0.95 precision. SAPS-Net provides a validated, scalable, and efficient tool for high-resolution litter mapping, optimizing cleanup logistics, and informing environmental policy. © 2026 American Chemical Society

title: Detection versus Instance Segmentation for Multi-Species Malaria Diagnosis: A Head-to-Head Comparison and Multi-Dataset Validation of YOLOv12 Architectures with Small Object Optimization
authors: Issah A.T.; Seidu I.; Mukamakuza C.
abstract: Automated malaria parasite detection using deep learning holds promise for addressing diagnostic gaps in resource-limited settings, yet most studies rely on single-dataset evaluations that fail to capture real-world variability. In this work, we rigorously validate YOLOv12-based architectures for malaria detection across diverse geographic and institutional contexts. We introduce a dual-head architecture combining instance segmentation with a high-resolution P2 detection head to target tiny ring-stage parasites. Our evaluation on a diverse Rwandan thick-smear dataset (2,739 images) and two external datasets from Ghana (Lacuna) and Nigeria (FASTMAL) reveals critical insights into model robustness. While the proposed YOLOv12-Seg-N-P2 model achieves state-of-the-art internal performance (mAP@50 0.888) and significantly improves detection of challenging P. vivax (+10.9%) and P. falciparum ring forms, external validation exposes severe domain shift, with performance dropping by > 80% on unseen datasets. We further demonstrate that while P2 heads enhance morphological precision on source data, they reduce zero-shot generalization, likely by overfitting to dataset-specific acquisition characteristics. We additionally evaluate white blood cell (WBC)-anchored stain normalization and pixel-scale rescaling as inference-time domain adaptation strategies. While WBC detection improves substantially (up to +45% on Lacuna), P. falciparum detection remains critically low across both external datasets despite partial recovery on FASTMAL, confirming that preprocessing-based adaptation alone is insufficient for reliable cross-site parasite detection. © 2026 CC-BY 4.0, A.T. title: Comparative Evaluation of CNN and Transformer-Based Instance Segmentation Architectures for Whitefly Detection in Citrus Crops
authors: Manzano-Soto L.; Fernández-Campusano C.; Verdejo-Fredes H.; Becker C.; Carrasco R.
abstract: This study focuses on the detection of pests in citrus fruits using computer vision (CV) techniques and image detection technologies based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Early detection enables pest control, reduces the use of pesticides, and generates alerts for the inspection of surrounding areas. One of the models used is You Only Look Once (YOLO), which is based on a single-stage CNN. This model is fast, resource-efficient, and has low latency, enabling it to run on a personal computer. Another type of neural network is based on the vision transformer, a paradigm that requires more hardware resources than YOLO but offers greater precision. Therefore, a comparison is carried out between CNN models to evaluate their precision and demonstrate that YOLO is an excellent option compared to vision transformer-based models, which are more resource-intensive. Through the capture of images in the field, it will be shown that the difference in precision compared to other models that are more demanding in terms of hardware is minimal. The study also reveals that all the models assessed have difficulties in detecting small objects, suggesting a need to improve this through software techniques or hardware enhancements, such as the optics of drone lenses. A wide-angle lens could be used for preliminary detection, and another with a higher zoom for confirmation and the detection of small insects, thereby facilitating its adoption where computational resources are limited. © 2026 by the authors.

title: OPPFormer: Wavelet-Enhanced Object Prior Perception for Underwater Instance Segmentation in Ocean Internet of Things
authors: Lv S.; Zhang S.; Wei Y.
abstract: Underwater instance segmentation is a fundamental task for underwater visual perception in the Ocean Internet of Things (OIoT), supporting applications such as marine ecological monitoring, underwater robot navigation, seabed exploration, and underwater object analysis. However, accurate underwater instance segmentation remains challenging due to severe visual degradation caused by light attenuation, scattering, color distortion, low contrast, and blurred object boundaries. These degradations make it difficult to distinguish individual object instances from complex underwater backgrounds, especially in scenarios involving small objects, occlusions, dense distributions, and weak boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose OPPFormer, a wavelet-enhanced object prior perception framework for underwater instance segmentation. OPPFormer adopts a transformer-based backbone for multi-scale feature extraction and builds upon the Mask2Former decoder for instance mask prediction. To enhance foreground perception, we design an Object Prior Perception (OPP) branch to model foreground-background responses, guiding the network to focus on underwater objects while suppressing background interference. In addition, a Wavelet-Enhanced Block(WE-Block) is introduced to strengthen boundary and texture representations in the frequency domain, thereby improving robustness under degraded underwater imaging conditions. Extensive experiments on the USIS10K and UIIS datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with the baseline, OPPFormer achieves AP gains of 2.0 on USIS10K and 1.9 on UIIS, showing improved localization, boundary recovery, and instance-level segmentation performance in challenging underwater scenes. © 2014 IEEE.

title: Feature Fusion to Improve YOLOv8 for Segmenting and Classifying Aerial Images of Tree Crowns
authors: Z. Sun; B. Xue; M. Zhang; J. Schindler
src: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
abstract: Instance segmentation techniques based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is a vital tool for accurately identifying and segmenting individual tree crowns, which plays an essential role in environmental monitoring and forest management. In varied rural landscapes, canopy imagery often includes a mix of tiny, small, and medium tree objects scattered across diverse terrains, from standalone trees to densely clustered forest stands. This variability poses significant challenges to traditional instance segmentation methods. To achieve this, we introduce a new method named YOLOv8-FF, which incorporates a feature fusion (FF) technique based on the YOLOv8 architecture. We first design a network architecture based on YOLOv8 that is optimized for the characteristics of our dataset, enabling effective segmentation of densely distributed tiny and small tree crowns. Moreover, YOLOv8-FF incorporates a FF mechanism that includes both cross-scale and same-scale fusion methods, enhancing the model’s ability to integrate information across different layers and scales, thereby improving segmentation performance. We incorporate Sparse Large Kernel Network, whose large convolution kernel can effectively extract key features, helping the model capture richer and deeper global information in the image. Experimental results on the tree crown dataset demonstrate that YOLOv8-FF outperforms several recent peer competitors, making it a promising tool for accurate and efficient tree crown instance segmentation.

title: Real-Time Instance Segmentation for Object Scale Diversity
authors: Y. Chen; Y. Zhao; J. Zhong
src: 2025 IEEE 6th International Conference on Computer, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence (ICCBD+AI)
abstract: Achieving an optimal trade-off between inference latency and segmentation accuracy is paramount for safety-critical applications, such as autonomous driving and maritime surveillance. However, current real-time frameworks largely rely on static receptive fields that are ill-equipped to handle significant object scale variations, frequently resulting in performance degradation when detecting diminutive targets. To mitigate this representational bias, we present a novel Scale-Equalization Decoder (SED). Unlike traditional approaches, SED dynamically modulates local feature responses within shallow layers to equilibrate the semantic weight of objects regardless of their size. By effectively amalgamating these rectified features with deep semantic information, our method significantly improves segmentation fidelity without incurring substantial computational costs. Comprehensive experiments on standard benchmarks (MS COCO, Cityscapes) and remote sensing datasets (SSDD, HRSID) demonstrate that our proposed architecture outperforms contemporary real-time baselines, exhibiting superior capability in small-object detection within complex environments.

title: Automated Zebrafish Spine Scoring System Based on Instance Segmentation

title: An Asymmetric Dual-Domain Weighted Information Fusion Method for Small Object Segmentation in Pathological Images
authors: H. Lin; T. Xie
src: 2025 7th International Conference on Internet of Things, Automation and Artificial Intelligence (IoTAAI)
abstract: Instance segmentation is crucial in computer vision, underpinning applications like road recognition and pathological image analysis. The main difficulties in segmenting small objects arise from low foreground-background contrast, poor separability between adhesive instances, and irregular shapes, leading to missed segmentation, under-segmentation and mis-segmentation. To address these challenges, this work proposes an asymmetric dual-domain weighted information fusion strategy based on contrast and separability enhancement. It enhances the model’s sensitivity to boundary details and low-contrast features by applying asymmetric feature reorganization in the spatial domain and asymmetric competitive weighting in the channel domain. Specifically, the strategy first utilizes hierarchical residual connections to establish unidirectional dependencies, enabling fine-grained spatial feature extraction and fusion. Then, a Softmax-based competitive mechanism assigns non-uniform channel attention weights by fusing global and local features, thereby achieving discriminative information weighting. Furthermore, to alleviate missed and under-segmentation, we introduce a Multi-scale Segmentation Head that applies independent supervision at each decoder output, with ground truth masks at corresponding resolutions. This independent supervision computes the loss at each scale, ensuring that the model preserves effective features and mitigates detail loss. Extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: A Lightweight Model Based on Agent-Attention for Real-Time Instance Segmentation
authors: L. Sun; Y. Li; G. Liu; X. Chen; H. Ning
src: 2025 17th International Conference on Signal Processing Systems (ICSPS)
abstract: Recently, Transformer-based instance segmentation methods have demonstrated remarkable potential, even surpassing traditional convolutional approaches. However, their complex computation and memory consumption remain challenging for real-time applications. In this paper, we introduce FastInst-AA, a lightweight model designed for real-time instance segmentation based on the Agent-Attention mechanism. The proposed model employs a Pyramid Pooling Module-Feature Pyramid Network (PPM-FPN) to extract multi-scale features and learnable tokens of target instances. An Agent-Attention Transformer then assigns each pixel block in the image to a target instance using a querybased approach. Unlike traditional self-attention, the AgentAttention mechanism eliminates the need for pairwise similarity computations between Q and K, reducing the attention mechanism’s complexity from quadratic to linear. Experimental results on the COCO dataset demonstrate that FastInst-AA achieves an average precision (AP) of 38.2 at a real-time speed of 40.2 FPS, surpassing most state-of-the-art real-time instance segmentation models in both speed and accuracy.

title: Segmentation-Based Detection of Oyster Mushroom Caps Using YOLOv8 for Smart Cultivation Monitoring

abstract: Oyster mushroom (Pleurotus Ostreatus) cultivation is gaining popularity due to its short growth cycle, rich nutrient contents and easy growing. A manual-annotated polygon-based annotation dataset has been used to train the YOLOv8 segmentation model. This model also provides infestation detection which enables the system to have targeted treatment at an early stage to minimize overall damage and maintain the productivity of the cultivation environment. The problem to be addressed through this study is to determine the optimal harvesting time for oyster mushrooms. This is to prevent overgrown mushroom, contamination and infestation that lead to poor quality of mushroom production. Suitable design of computer vision model is the proposed solution to provide a real-time visual tracking pipeline for oyster mushroom growth monitoring. The trained model achieves mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 91.9% and (mAP@0.5–0.95) of 79.1%. The model’s ability to mask a single mushroom cap size area was established using test images of different classes, from the beginning stage of small-cap size to ready harvest till overgrown large mushroom cap and that resulted in detection. This work explains the setup of the model pipeline which consists of data preparation, model training, and inference. Early post-processing was explored, and the trained model is set out to build a reliable detection framework to be used as a reference point for future maturity analysis, tracking, and harvesting reasoning. The results demonstrate the potential of using deep learning segmentation in mushroom cultivation to enable scalable low-labour monitoring.

title: Improvement of Tiny Crack Detection Accuracy in High Resolution Road Image Captured by Drone

title: FSD V2: Improving Fully Sparse 3D Object Detection With Virtual Voxels
authors: L. Fan; F. Wang; N. Wang; Z. Zhang
src: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: LiDAR-based fully sparse architecture has gained increasing attention. FSDv1 stands out as a representative work, achieving impressive efficacy and efficiency, albeit with intricate structures and handcrafted designs. In this paper, we present FSDv2, an evolution that aims to simplify the previous FSDv1 and eliminate the ad-hoc heuristics in its handcrafted instance-level representation, thus promoting better universality. To this end, we introduce virtual voxels, taking over the clustering-based instance segmentation in FSDv1. Virtual voxels not only address the notorious issue of the Center Feature Missing in fully sparse detectors but also endow the framework with a more elegant and streamlined approach. Besides, we develop a suite of components to complement the virtual voxel mechanism, including a virtual voxel encoder, a virtual voxel mixer, and a virtual voxel assignment strategy. We conduct experiments on three large-scale datasets: Waymo Open Dataset, Argoverse 2 dataset, and nuScenes dataset. Our results showcase state-of-the-art performance on all three datasets, highlighting the superiority of FSDv2 in long-range scenarios and its universality in achieving competitive performance across diverse scenarios. Moreover, we provide comprehensive experimental analysis to understand the workings of FSDv2.

title: Open-World Video Panoptic Segmentation for Aerial Perception using Foundation Models
authors: N. -G. Boncea; V. Chiciudean; F. Oniga; S. Nedevschi
src: 2025 IEEE 21st International Conference on Intelligent Computer Communication and Processing (ICCP)
abstract: Accurate scene understanding from low-altitude aerial video cameras is a prerequisite for autonomous urban drones. However, current methods are confined to closed taxonomies and struggle with the high object density, scale variation, and viewpoint changes typical of UAV footage. We propose, to our knowledge, the first open-world video panoptic segmentation pipeline tailored for aerial perception, driven primarily by foundation models and enhanced with domain-specific pre- and post-processing filters. Built around the Grounded Segment Anything Model (Grounded SAM), our pipeline leverages the Decoupled Video Segmentation (DEVA) architecture. This enables scalable and memory-efficient temporal propagation, supporting robust segmentation and tracking over long video sequences with dense object distributions. A key innovation is an adaptive slicing mechanism inspired by the Slicing Aided Hyper Inference (SAHI) model, which adjusts the granularity of windowing based on spatial location. It applies finer slices to the upper part of the frame and coarser ones to the lower part, improving the detection of small aerial objects without compromising inference speed. Additionally, we introduce a class-aware slicing strategy that dynamically resizes SAHI windows depending on the predicted object class size, enabling effective segmentation of both small and large objects in the same scene while preserving open-vocabulary generalization. The use of Light HQ-SAM ensures efficient segmentation with minimal resource overhead, allowing the system to handle long videos with high object density. Operating fully autonomously, the pipeline extracts relevant textual labels directly from input frames using Llama 3.2 Vision, which seamlessly guides the segmentation and tracking components without requiring manual input.

title: FGISN: Fine-Grained Instance Segmentation Networks in Cluttered Environments Based on Multiscale Fusion With RGBD Sensor
authors: H. Wang; J. Deng; C. Liu; J. Tan; J. Hu
abstract: Three-dimensional instance segmentation has developed rapidly in the field of autonomous driving, with recent research primarily focusing on outdoor large-scale scenes. However, in robot operation environments characterized by target stacking, occlusion, and clutter, such studies often suffer from instance confusion, information loss of small and occluded targets, leading to insufficient segmentation accuracy. This makes them unsuitable for 3-D instance segmentation tasks in robotic manipulation scenarios. To address the challenges, we innovatively propose an adaptive fine-grained instance segmentation network (FGISN) based on a monocular depth sensor system, enabling precise object segmentation in complex scenes. The core of FGISN mainly comprises two components: category-space hybrid enhanced upsampler (CSHEU) and instance scale-aware attention fusion (SAAF) module. CSHEU employs a hybrid interpolation strategy that fuses semantic and spatial feature information to suppress noise interference from neighboring objects and resolve information confusion between different instances. SAAF leverages a cross-scale attention mechanism and a multiscale fusion method to achieve maximum sampling of information for small and occluded objects. Extensive experiments conducted on public datasets fully confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: OV-BIS: Open-Vocabulary Boundary Guide Zero-Shot 3D Instance Segmentation
authors: T. Yi; S. Wang; Z. Zhang; C. Wang; D. Yan; R. Xu; E. Chen
abstract: Open vocabulary 3D instance segmentation aims to align 3D instance segmentation results with natural language text, thereby achieving semantic prediction without relying on predefined class labels for specific scenes, which has been widely used in the field of multimedia. Current open vocabulary 3D instance segmentation methods mainly rely on 2D masks provided by various 2D segmentation foundation models. However, in complex scenes, the calculation of 2D masks often struggles to balance over-segmentation of large objects and under-segmentation of small objects. In this paper, we introduce OV-BIS, a novel zero-shot open vocabulary 3D instance segmentation method that leverages instance boundary information to improve 3D semantic segmentation performance. The key insight of our method is that the edge map as 3D boundary projection is suitable for multi-scale tasks and capable of compensating for the weakness of 2D masks in multi-scale adaptability for complex scenes. Our method aggregates multiview edge maps and 2D masks, iteratively guiding the merging of over-segmented point clouds with regions growing to cluster 3D primitives into distinct 3D instances. By projecting 3D instances onto images and using CLIP to calculate semantic features from multiple perspectives with an outliers filter, 3D semantic instance segmentation has been achieved. Experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method.

This research addresses this gap by conducting a unified analysis of the performance characteristics of YOLOv8 alongside Mask R-CNN and two variation models, ResNeXt-based Mask R-CNN as well as Cascade Mask R-CNN (HTC), for instance, segmentation in urban scene understanding. Both accuracy performance metrics, including precision, recall, F1 score, mAP, and IoU, and computational speed metric, inference time, along with FPS, were evaluated on the Cityscapes dataset for this study. title: v-CLR: View-Consistent Learning for Open-World Instance Segmentation
authors: C. -B. Zhang; J. Ni; Y. Zhong; K. Han
src: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenging problem of open-world instance segmentation. Existing works have shown that vanilla visual networks are biased toward learning appearance information, e.g., texture, to recognize objects. This implicit bias causes the model to fail in detecting novel objects with unseen textures in the open-world setting. To address this challenge, we propose a learning framework, called view-Consistent LeaRning (v-CLR), which aims to enforce the model to learn appearance-invariant representations for robust instance segmentation. In v-CLR, we first introduce additional views for each image, where the texture undergoes significant alterations while preserving the image’s underlying structure. We then encourage the model to learn the appearance-invariant representation by enforcing the consistency between object features across different views, for which we obtain class-agnostic object proposals using off-the-shelf unsupervised models that possess strong object-awareness. These proposals enable cross-view object feature matching, greatly reducing the appearance dependency while enhancing the object-awareness. We thoroughly evaluate our method on public benchmarks under both cross-class and cross-dataset settings, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Project page: https://visual-ai.github.io/vclr

abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation (OV-3DIS), which aims to segment and classify objects beyond predefined categories, is a critical capability for embodied AI applications. To address these limitations, we propose an OV-3DIS framework guided by contextual information. Subsequently, we design a Semantic Reasoning Module, which selects the best viewpoint for each instance and constructs three $2 D$ contextaware representations. The representations are processed using Multimodal Large Language Models with Chain-ofThought prompting to enhance semantic inference. Notably, our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the ScanNet200 and Replica datasets, demonstrating superior open-vocabulary segmentation capabilities. Moreover, preliminary implementation in real-world scenarios verifies our method's robustness and accuracy, highlighting its potential for embodied AI tasks such as object-driven navigation. title: STFormer: Spatial-Temporal-Aware Transformer for Video Instance Segmentation

src: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
abstract: Video instance segmentation (VIS) is a challenging task, requiring handling object classification, segmentation, and tracking in videos. Existing Transformer-based VIS approaches have shown remarkable success, combining encoded features and instance queries as decoder inputs. However, their decoder inputs are low-resolution due to computational cost, resulting in a loss of fine-grained information, sensitivity to background interference, and poor handling of small objects. Moreover, the queries are randomly initialized without location information, hindering convergence efficiency and accurate object instance localization. To address these issues, we propose a novel VIS approach, STFormer, with a spatial-temporal feature aggregation (STFA) module and spatial-temporal-aware Transformer (STT). Specifically, STFA obtains robust high-resolution masked features efficiently for the decoder, while STT’s location-guided instance query (LGIQ) improves initial instance queries. STFormer preserves more fine-grained information, improves convergence efficiency, and localizes object instance features accurately. Extensive experiments on YouTube-VIS 2019, YouTube-VIS 2021, and OVIS datasets show that STFormer outperforms mainstream VIS methods.

abstract: To address feature mismatching and localization degradation caused by dynamic objects in visual SLAM systems operating under dynamic environments, this paper proposes DySeG-SLAM—a dynamic SLAM framework integrating semantic-geometric constraints. Second, a pyramid iterative Lucas-Kanade (LK) optical flow method is implemented for multi-scale feature tracking in static regions. Third, a multi-view geometric approach combining disparity angle analysis and depth projection error evaluation is introduced to identify dynamic objects parallel to camera motion. Finally, a dynamic probability model incorporating historical states, epipolar constraints, and multi-view geometry is established to stabilize detection consistency against single-frame errors. Evaluations on the TUM dataset demonstrate that DySeG-SLAM achieves superior localization accuracy compared to ORB-SLAM2 in dynamic scenarios, with translation and rotation errors reduced by over 92%. title: DBN-YOLO: A Dynamic Sparse Deformable Instance Segmentation Method for Sonar Images
authors: Z. Chen; L. Li; J. Tang; H. Qiu
src: 2025 IEEE 12th Joint International Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence Conference (ITAIC)
abstract: Underwater sonar image instance segmentation is a crucial component for tasks such as marine resource exploration, underwater communication and navigation, and marine environmental monitoring. Existing sonar image segmentation models primarily rely on traditional machine learning methods, which face challenges in adapting to the complex characteristics of underwater sonar images. Underwater sonar image targets often exhibit complex scale variations and geometric deformations, which can pose challenges for segmentation models to accurately capture the details of all targets, especially for small objects. Additionally, these targets may possess low contrast and blurry edges, leading to foreground and background mixing during the training process, resulting in the loss of target features. Moreover, there is a class imbalance issue between the target and background categories, which can lead to the generation of blurry or inaccurate segmentation results by the segmentation models. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper proposes DBN-YOLO: a dynamic sparse attention-based deformable underwater sonar image instance segmentation model, built upon the existing YOLOv5-seg instance segmentation model. Firstly, the Deformable Convolution Network (DCN) is introduced. By incorporating learnable offsets, DCN can adaptively adjust the sampling positions of convolution kernels to better accommodate deformations and geometric variations of the targets. This helps improve the segmentation model's ability to accurately capture object boundaries, thereby enhancing the segmentation effectiveness. Next, the BiFormer attention module is introduced. It employs a dual-layer routing attention module to compute key regions at a coarse granularity and perform attention interaction at a fine granularity. This enhances the foreground weights and suppresses the background weights, enabling the model to focus more on the targets and improve segmentation accuracy and effectiveness. Lastly, the Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) loss is introduced to alleviate the sensitivity of the original Intersection over Union (IOU) metric to positional deviations of small targets and mitigate the impact of imbalanced positive and negative samples on target segmentation. The experimental results illustrate that the proposed DBN-YOLO mode improves the recall rate by 3.9% and the mAP@0.5 by 3.1% on the SCTD-seg dataset.
