title: Robust Cell Segmentation for Size Distribution Estimation via Synthetic-Data Training
authors: Kim H.B.; Lee C.; Lee N.; Han H.; Park C.; Hong M.S.
abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are biodegradable and biocompatible plastics, yet large-scale production remains limited by costly batch operations and the lack of online analytical tools. Monitoring cell size distribution serves as a strong surrogate for intracellular PHA content, but training robust cell segmentation models for industrial bioprocesses requires extensive manual annotation, which is highly labor-intensive and impractical for densely populated microscopy images. To address this critical bottleneck, an annotation-free cell segmentation and size estimation pipeline tailored for real time monitoring is presented. Rather than relying on architectural modifications, this framework introduces a system-level automated training strategy: individual cells are automatically extracted from diluted-sample microscopy images using edge enhancement and rule-based binarization, then augmented and composited onto heterogeneous backgrounds to emulate the texture of undiluted, dense cultures. This fully synthetic data generation eliminates the need for manual labeling while enabling robust training of instance segmentation models. When implemented using a Mask R-CNN backbone, the proposed pipeline consistently tracks flow cytometry forward-scatter (FSC) distribution trends under diverse imaging conditions and achieves higher correlation with FSC data compared to Cellpose and CellSAM, representative foundation models for cell segmentation. This annotation-free methodology provides a practical and reliable automated online monitoring solution for intelligent PHA manufacturing. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Pointer Pressure Gauge Reading Recognition System Based on Lightweight Multitask Interactive Network for Intelligent Robotic-Assisted Measurement
authors: Guo J.; Long X.; Zhao X.; Li Y.; Liu H.; Huang H.
src: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Due to the low efficiency of manual inspection of pointer pressure gauges, numerous computer vision-based automatic reading recognition systems have been proposed in recent years. However, most existing work primarily focuses on using cameras or inspection robots for daily monitoring of gauges. Periodic calibration of gauges is equally important, as it ensures their optimal performance and imposes stricter precision requirements on inspections. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight multitask interactive network (LMI-Net) and develops an intelligent robotic-assisted measurement system. LMI-Net, which generates a large number of feature maps through computationally inexpensive operation of a lightweight module, realizes multiple tasks via keypoint detection and instance segmentation branches. The keypoint detection branch identifies the position of the main scale and the center of the gauge, while the instance segmentation branch generates a segmentation mask of the pointer. Through our proposed multiple feature fusion (MFF) reading method, the value and order of the main scale are identified, the segmentation mask of the pointer is fitted to a straight line using a regional interpolation linear fitting method, and on the basis of geometric relationships, these pieces of feature information are fused to obtain a reading. Experimental results on a dataset containing multiple types of gauge demonstrate that with the proposed method, the reading error is controlled to within ±1/5 of the minimum resolution interval, which complies with the verification regulation for pointer pressure gauges. Note to Practitioners—This work is motivated by the time-consuming and error-prone process of periodic calibration and daily monitoring of pointer pressure gauges in industrial settings. We introduce LMI-Net, a compact multitask vision network that simultaneously detects gauge keypoints and segments the pointer mask, and show how it can be integrated with an automated robotic inspection station to deliver fully automatic readings with accuracy within ±1/5 of the gauge resolution. Using lightweight GhostConv and hybrid convolution-attention modules, LMI-Net runs at more than 24 FPS on modest edge-compute hardware, making it suitable for retrofitting existing gauge-holding fixtures or inspection robots. In addition, this method can also be applied directly to obtain the pressure gauge readings taken by the camera. The perspective correction algorithm proposed in this paper can make good use of the information of key points to correct the image. Previous experiments have demonstrated that accurate readings of pointer pressure gauges can be obtained in both periodic calibration and daily monitoring scenarios, validating the feasibility of the proposed method. However, further testing in real industrial environments is necessary to evaluate its robustness and generalizability in practical applications. Future work will focus on integrating the system with mobile measurement platforms and extending its application to other types of pointer-based instrument. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

abstract: Existing machine vision-based tool condition monitoring (MV-TCM) methods are limited to instantaneous wear quantification from single images, lacking the capability for temporal-sequence-based prediction of future wear progression. title: Investigating Instance Segmentation Performance in Relation to Dataset Composition and Quality
authors: Bell M.; Vitali R.V.
abstract: High-mix, low-volume (HMLV) manufacturing faces persistent barriers to deploying deep learning-based perception due to the cost and effort of collecting large, labeled image datasets. This study investigates how training dataset composition, specifically the proportion of real images and the use of synthetic and/or augmented supplementation, relates to instance segmentation performance on real images. Using the Sandcast Images for Foundry Automation (SIFA) dataset, a fixed test set of 108 representative real images was extracted and held constant across all trained models. From the remaining real, augmented, and synthetic images, training pools were generated for each supplementation strategy and ratio of real data. For every condition, 3 random seeds were used to split each pool into 756 training images and 216 validation images. YOLOv8 instance segmentation models initialized with MS COCO weights were evaluated on the same real image test set. Objective image quality metrics were computed for each training subset to characterize dataset structure and relate these properties to model fitness. Under the controlled conditions of this study, introducing a small fraction of real data was associated with substantial performance gains, after which improvements diminished. Datasets combining synthetic and augmented images with limited real subsets generally achieved performance comparable to the all real baseline. Overall, the results suggest effective training datasets benefit from structured, complementary variation that remains anchored to the real image domain, highlighting pathways toward more data efficient model development for HMLV applications.  © 2013 IEEE.

title: Edge-deployable instance segmentation framework for densely overlapping embryo-retained rice grains in industrial processing

abstract: The realization of instance segmentation of high-density adhered overlapping rice grains is very important for online quality detection and intelligent sorting in modern rice milling technology. However, existing methods still struggle with severe adhesion, occlusion, and overlap in industrial environments, while annotating densely packed grain images remains extremely time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address these challenges, this research proposes an efficient densely overlapping grain segmentation framework, together with a practical data construction strategy. A semi-automatic annotation process built upon the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is first introduced, reducing the manual annotation workload by approximately 83% while maintaining high-quality mask boundaries. The segmentation architecture further designs three collaborative modules, namely an Adaptive Feature Aggregation Network for enhancing multi-scale context encoding, a Multi-Scale Sequence Fusion Module using three-dimensional convolution to explicitly model inter-scale dependencies, and a Hybrid Weighted Feature Fusion Module for achieving robust feature propagation. Soft Non-Maximum Suppression is additionally applied during inference to better distinguish overlapping grains. Experiments on a dedicated embryo-retained rice dataset containing 1046 images and 78,422 annotated instances demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an optimal performance of 98.0% mAP50val and 85.1% mAP50:95val with only 2.37 M parameters. When deployed to a standard edge computing device and running at FP16 precision, the model achieves a real-time processing ability of 18.87 FPS. title: AI-enabled digital twin framework for reconfigurable robotic palletizing of irregularly shaped products

abstract: Palletizing in intralogistics and manufacturing remains particularly challenging when dealing with irregularly shaped products, large variant sets, and frequently changing customer orders. abstract: Accurate monitoring of bubble population and bubble size distribution (BSD) is essential for intelligent froth flotation control, yet remains challenging due to the dense, semi-transparent, and visually ambiguous nature of flotation froths. On a self built dataset containing 1300 images, this system achieved an average accuracy of 97.66% in dial detection (mAP@75) The average absolute error (MAE) of the readings is only 2.9129% (relative to full scale), meeting industrial grade standards. The novelty of the proposed model design lies in the coupling of instance-segmentation-based dial extraction, RANSAC-based geometric correction, polar-coordinate pointer localization, and local fitting-based reading mapping. Instead of directly estimating the pointer angle in the original image, the proposed method converts the reading problem into a more stable coordinate-localization problem in the unfolded polar space. This design reduces the influence of camera tilt, dial deformation, partial occlusion, and OCR errors, and provides a reliable solution for automatic pressure-gauge reading in industrial environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: MV-Seg-Grasp: Multiview Spatial Feature-Fused Segmentation for 6-DoF Robotic Grasp
authors: Ren L.; Liu S.; Dong J.
abstract: Vision-based grasping is a widely adopted approach in robotic manipulation, particularly in complex multitarget industrial scenarios with significant practical applications. The emergence of embodied intelligence significantly accelerates the advancement of vision-based intelligent grasping technologies. However, most existing methods rely on single-view visual perception, which often fails to adequately capture complete visual information of target objects. This incomplete capturing problem is mainly caused by object occlusion, object stacking, and edge occlusion, which significantly limits effective grasp in stacking and occluded scenario. To address these challenges, a multiview spatial feature-fused segmentation grasp framework is proposed, incorporating both a multiview fused segmentation module and a multiscale grasp detection module. The multiview fused segmentation module can achieve the fusion and segmentation of multiview point clouds. The multiscale grasp detection module utilizes multiscale feature extraction and fusion to obtain high-quality grasp results. Experimental results in both simulation and physical world finally demonstrate that the proposed framework enhances grasp success rate in stacking and occluded scenes while improving performance in simpler scenarios. © 1996-2012 IEEE.

title: Research on AGV Driving Stability from Multi-Modal Crack Perception to Vibration Constraint Speed Decision
authors: Chen P.; Yang Y.; Zhou C.; Zhang X.; Li J.; Liu Y.; Liao X.
abstract: Pavement cracks pose significant challenges to the driving stability and operational safety of automated guided vehicles (AGV) in industrial and logistics environments. The complex geometry of cracks and their nonlinear coupling with vehicle dynamics make conventional rule-based or single-modal approaches insufficient for reliable engineering decision-making. To address this issue, this study proposes an artificial intelligence–driven multi-modal perception and engineering analysis framework for AGV speed optimization under representative operating conditions. From the artificial intelligence perspective, an improved lightweight instance segmentation model based on YOLO11 is developed by integrating a dynamic upsampling strategy, a hybrid multi-scale feature representation module, and a large-kernel attention mechanism, enabling robust and fine-grained crack extraction in complex pavement scenes. In addition, a multi-modal learning strategy is adopted to fuse two-dimensional visual features with three-dimensional point cloud-derived geometric parameters, allowing accurate quantification of crack width, depth, and surface damage. From the engineering analysis perspective, the relationship between AI-extracted crack geometric characteristics and AGV dynamic responses is established to investigate the influence of pavement defects on vehicle vibration behavior. A triaxial vibration acquisition system is constructed under controlled experimental conditions, and the relationship between crack severity, vibration characteristics, and driving speed is quantitatively analyzed. Based on vibration constraints, a hierarchical speed optimization strategy is formulated for different crack levels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate crack perception and effective geometric feature characterization, providing a quantitative basis for AGV speed adjustment under different pavement conditions. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Lightweight deep learning framework for quality assessment of rolled fondant
authors: Rodríguez E.; Pauccar G.; Carrizales J.; Inga Espinoza C.H.
abstract: Inconsistent quality and operator subjectivity in rolled fondant production hinder process standardization. This study presents an integrated vision-based quality verification system for the nondestructive assessment of sheeted fondant, focusing on color class, spatial uniformity, and surface porosity. The framework combines a calibrated sRGB to CIELAB imaging pipeline with three custom ultra lightweight deep learning models (19k to 766k parameters). To ensure statistical rigor, performance was evaluated using 50 captures per model to establish 95 percent Confidence Intervals, and benchmarked against YOLOv5, YOLOv8, and YOLOv11 architectures on a Raspberry Pi5. The proposed models achieved superior metrological reliability. The classification models reached 100 percent accuracy and perfect uniformity estimation within the highly controlled radiometric dataset, overcoming the low prediction confidence and high false positive rates of the heavily parameterized YOLO networks. Furthermore, the custom fully convolutional network accurately quantified surface porosity (38.27 percent), avoiding above 95 percent saturation errors of the YOLO segmentation heads and demonstrating that continuous micro-textural defects require semantic rather than instance segmentation. While multi second inference times currently restrict deployment to final state processes rather than continuous high speed inline monitoring, these results validate a highly repeatable, parameter efficient, and low-cost metrological tool for smart food manufacturing environments. title: A geometry-driven pipeline for particle size distribution analysis of contacting particles in complex industrial settings
authors: Lu J.; Wang Y.; Lu M.; Wang D.; Pan M.; Jiang H.; Duan C.
abstract: Particle size distribution (PSD) is a key performance indicator in mineral processing and comminution, directly affecting crushing, screening, dense medium separation, and product quality control. In industrial vision scenarios, segmentation errors can be exacerbated by complex and uneven backgrounds, widespread particle adhesion, and harsh operating conditions, leading to limitations in measurement reliability during particle sizing and PSD estimation. To address this issue, the present study focuses on investigating foreground extraction, adhesion-aware instance segmentation, and PSD estimation using high-resolution depth data acquired through line-laser profilometry. Experiments were conducted on dry gold ore particles with particle sizes ranging from 3–25 mm under controlled sampling and laser-scanning conditions. From the perspective of error propagation, a geometry-driven PSD analysis pipeline was developed without relying on large-scale training data. Normal-variation-based and autoencoder-based foreground extraction methods were evaluated, and a depth-peak-guided watershed instance segmentation method (DepthPeak) was introduced. The consistency of different equivalent particle size definitions in volume-based PSD statistics was analyzed. Experimental results show that the normal-variation-based foreground extraction method achieves an average Intersection over Union of approximately 0.880 and an F1-score of approximately 0.936. Conversely, the proposed DepthPeak attains an average F1-score of approximately 0.918 across multiple particle-size ranges. Compared with projected-area-based and major-axis-based size definitions, the volume-equivalent particle size exhibits higher consistency with ground-truth annotations, with volume distribution deviations of less than 2 percentage points across all size classes. This study validates a geometry-driven PSD analysis workflow under controlled sampling and line-laser acquisition conditions, demonstrating stable and consistent PSD estimation using gold ore particles. title: Dual-channel graph neural network for dental 3D point cloud model segmentation
authors: Guo P.; Lu Y.; Yang C.; Wang W.; Wu H.; Zhao Z.; Elloumi M.; Touti E.
abstract: By using 3D teeth segmentation via Intraoral scan, digitized dentistry becomes possible and easy. 3D instance segmentation is complex due to the complicated architecture of intraoral scan teeth, lack of boundary between adjacent teeth, and point cloud data noise. Primary methods cannot simultaneously obtain local and global connection data to the dental arches in areas with overlapping archform and crowded arch dimensions, resulting in the errors that are found there. To address the multi-scale representation gap and overcome the limitation of single-scale feature learning, dual-Graph Fusion Network (DGF-Net) can be used to reduce the gap between multi-scale and single-scale graph feature learning. A key feature of DGF-Net is its dual-graph design, which comprises of two channels for graph processing. Global graph channels are active in collecting topology and semantics, while local graph channels are active in collecting high resolution geometry. Under a trained fusion module both channels provide different feature detail information which is fused together. On comprehensive clinical dentistry point cloud dataset, the DGF-Net achieved 98.54% accuracy in segmentation and 97.89% Dice coefficient, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches. Through the accurate and stable nature of the DGF-Net model, various dental treatment scenarios can be efficiently realized, such as automated orthodontic simulation or precision manufacturing of patient-specific surgical guides, which enhances the efficiency and personalized nature of dental treatment. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Research on Multi-task Deep Learning Model for Detection, Segmentation and Ranging Based on Improved YOLOv8
authors: Li X.; Li Y.; Jiang Y.; Zhou Y.; Liu H.; Li J.
abstract: With the development of computer vision towards multi-task collaborative processing, traditional algorithms face significant challenges such as feature conflicts, information gaps, and insufficient real-time performance when dealing with tasks like detection, segmentation, and depth estimation simultaneously. To address this, this paper proposes an improved multi-task fusion scheme based on YOLOv8. By embedding a depth estimation module, an integrated algorithm framework with functions of object detection, instance segmentation, and monocular depth estimation is constructed. Leveraging the efficient feature extraction capability of the CSP backbone network, combined with multi-scale prediction and task-optimized loss functions, the framework demonstrates fundamental advantages in multi-task scenarios. The newly added depth estimation block, based on a CNN architecture, achieves feature sharing and complementary learning with detection and segmentation tasks through multi-scale feature fusion and self-supervised geometric constraints. Experimental results show that this multi-task integrated design expands the scene adaptability of YOLOv8, maintaining stable performance in scenarios such as daytime, nighttime, rain, snow, fog, and aerial targets. It provides a new idea of feature sharing and joint optimization for multi-task processing in computer vision, meeting the needs of multi-dimensional visual information processing in fields such as intelligent monitoring and industrial quality inspection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Instance segmentation and contrastive clustering techniques for white blood cell analysis
authors: Annadhani A.A.; Baalebail B.; Shetty D.K.; Hegde S.G.; Prabhu D.R.; Pullela P.K.; Malarout N.

title: Semi-Supervised Multimodal Individual Tree Crown Delineation via Crown Vertical Semantic Distillation With Selective Coupling
authors: Zhong X.; Song Z.; Fan X.; Tjahjadi T.; Ye Q.; Fu L.
src: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
abstract: Trees play a pivotal role in industrial processes by providing raw materials, such as timber and paper, while simultaneously contributing to sustainable practices through carbon dioxide sequestration and biodiversity support. Accurate monitoring of individual tree is crucial for managing forest resources and assessing environmental health. While unmanned aerial vehicle imagery provides an effective data source for this task, deep learning-based segmentation methods are often hindered by the prohibitive cost of generating the required instance-level annotations, particularly in dense forest scenes. To overcome this limitation, this article introduces a novel semi-supervised framework for individual tree segmentation. Recognizing that RGB imagery alone cannot capture vertical canopy structure, we integrate LiDAR-derived point cloud data through a multimodal fusion strategy that enhances the perceptual capabilities of the model. Specifically, our method leverages a canopy height model (CHM) to complement the rich textural details of RGB images. We propose an adaptive and efficient two-stage fusion architecture featuring a novel crown vertical semantic distillation with selective coupling module to integrate these heterogeneous data sources. Furthermore, we introduce a mask-guided training mechanism for tree crown to resolve the issue of inconsistent prediction of tree crown, which is common in transformer-based segmentation models. Extensive experiments conducted on four diverse datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method consistently outperforms existing semi-supervised methods based solely on RGB or CHM, as well as other multimodal semi-supervised instance segmentation methods. These results demonstrate its strong potential for accurate and annotation-efficient tree crown delineation. © 2008-2012 IEEE.

title: Instance Segmentation Models for Real-Time Progress Monitoring and Quality Control in Industrial Plant Construction
authors: Valladares-Poncela A.; Fernández-Caramés T.M.; Vilar-Martínez J.; Fraga-Lamas P.
src: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Applied Machine Intelligence and Informatics, SAMI
abstract: This paper proposes a progress monitoring solution through instance segmentation models for real-time production monitoring and quality control in industrial environments. The obtained results address digitalization challenges for automated monitoring of early-stage construction elements including foundation excavations, cast-in-place foundations, steel I-beam and lattice beam placement. Specifically, state-of-the-art instance segmentation architectures are evaluated, consisting of recent YOLO models (YOLOv8-seg, YOLOv11-seg) as well as established approaches (Mask R-CNN, Mask2Former) for industrial monitoring systems integration. An evaluation framework is established that integrates accuracy metrics (mask mean Average Precision (mAP)) with production efficiency measures including real-time processing (FPS) and deployment constraints. The performed analyses reveal accuracy-speed trade-offs essential for real-time applications in Industry 5.0 scenarios, where YOLO variants provide real-time monitoring capabilities and two-stage approaches deliver enhanced precision. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv8-seg variants achieve optimal performance with mAP@0.5:0.95 up to 54.09 % at 65 FPS, while YOLOv11-seg models provide superior parameter efficiency for resource-constrained environments. ©2026 IEEE.

title: Sparsifying Instance Segmentation Models for Efficient Vision-Based Industrial Recycling
authors: Neubauer M.; Özdenizci O.; Piater J.; Rueckert E.
abstract: Recycling is essential to the circular economy. However, efficient material sorting, particularly in steel scrap recycling, remains challenging due to material diversity and contamination. Visual computing via deep learning offers a significant promise in automation, with models such as YOLO and Mask R-CNN excelling in object detection and segmentation. However, high computational requirements often limit industrial deployment, which necessitates more efficient algorithmic solutions targeted for such applied machine learning problems. We introduce a novel approach to prune large image segmentation models based on instance-based importance scores (IBIS), specifically tailored to the problem of instance segmentation for automated steel scrap recycling. Our method identifies and prunes low priority parameters by leveraging parameter importance scores estimated by considering the presence of recyclable instances to be segmented in the frames. Moreover, we utilize a novel custom dataset constructed for the instance segmentation task during copper and steel scrap recycling, which involves recyclable objects of different sizes with various levels of difficulty. Our evaluations demonstrate promising computational efficiency gains without significant performance drops, while also enabling powerful out-of-distribution generalization, a game-changing capability. Finally, we discuss the potential of our work for real-world industrial applications, enabling resource-efficient deep learning deployment in large-scale automated sorting systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

abstract: Anthropogenic Marine Debris poses a significant threat to global aquatic ecosystems, leading to habitat destruction and the bioaccumulation of toxic substances. This study introduces a portable detection system utilizing YOLOv8 instance segmentation with modified parameters to identify five debris classes: metal cans, bottles, fishing nets, rubber footwear, and wrappers. title: Measurement-oriented micro-burr inspection using structure-aware imaging and segmentation

abstract: Micro-burrin spection is an important quality-control task during dental bur manufacturing. However, vision-based methods specifically developed for dental bur micro-burr inspection have received limited attention, particularly for real-time industrial applications. The extracted end-face images are subsequently processed by a YOLOv8-seg network to achieve pixel-level burr localization. The predicted segmentation masks are directly used to determine the presence or absence of burr defects for automated quality inspection. abstract: Bridge surface defect instance segmentation is a critical task for ensuring bridge safety, serving as a key driver for the industrialization and intelligent development of bridge engineering. abstract: Metal powders, as the medium in metal additive manufacturing, have their particle size, shape, and distribution characteristics directly influencing the quality of the final product. title: Real-Time Defect Detection in Automated Fiber Placement Using 3D Laser Scanning and Enhanced Instance Segmentation

abstract: Efficient detection of elongated defects (gaps and overlaps) in Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) is critical for enhancing the quality of carbon fiber composite components. First, high-precision point cloud data acquired via a 3D Laser Scanner is converted into depth images using a noise-resistant mapping algorithm, enabling submillimeter defect discrimination while correcting contour distortions. Second, we enhance the YOLOv11 instance segmentation model by introducing an Elongated Focal Loss (EFL) that emphasizes endpoint features and longitudinal continuity constraints, coupled with a three-stage dynamic training strategy for progressive performance optimization. title: Combining Open-Vocabulary Detection with Foundation Models for Object Recognition in an Industrial Bin Picking Context
authors: Chouaib Harik E.H.; Sigron P.; Hinderaker S.O.; Yagoubi M.R.
src: Proceedings - European Council for Modelling and Simulation, ECMS
abstract: Object recognition for industrial bin picking traditionally requires large annotated datasets and retraining when new parts are introduced. The sim-to-real gap further limits approaches that rely on synthetic training data alone. In this paper, we present an initial investigation into a three-stage pipeline that combines Grounding DINO (GroundingDINO) for open-vocabulary detection, the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) for instance segmentation, and a lightweight Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier operating on DINOv2 (self-supervised vision transformer) features. Only the classifier requires training on synthetic CAD renders; detection and segmentation rely entirely on the zero-shot capabilities of foundation models. This design isolates the sim-to-real gap to a single lightweight component operating on robust, pre-trained features. We evaluate our approach on the challenging T-LESS dataset, which features textureless, visually similar industrial objects with frequent symmetries, and achieve 70.0% class-level F1 on real images using only synthetic training data. title: Automated Approach for Clothing Insulation Estimation Using RGB Images and Deep Learning
authors: Bucarelli N.; Suri H.
src: Construction Research Congress 2026: Advanced Technologies, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Analytics in Construction - Selected papers from Construction Research Congress 2026
abstract: Occupant thermal comfort feedback is crucial for building control systems aiming to optimize both energy usage and occupant well-being. To predict individual thermal comfort autonomously (without direct occupant feedback), data-driven approaches have been proposed. They are based on factors affecting thermal comfort, such as indoor temperature, humidity, wind speed, activity level, and clothing insulation level (measured using the "clo"unit). However, clothing insulation is often neglected and assumed to be constant in comfort models due to data collection challenges in real-world settings. This research proposes an automated approach to estimate clo from RGB images using deep learning and the ISO 9920 mathematical formulation, which correlates clo values to garment body coverage and weights. To calculate coverage, instance segmentation models were used to identify (1) 11 garment types and their body areas; and (2) occupant body areas. Garment weights were determined from references in regulated standards. To test the approach, 175 garments from 60 images collected online were used. The proposed approach achieved 0.020 MAE and 78% R2 in estimating garment clo values. The approach could be used to enhance thermal comfort prediction through automated clothing insulation estimation. © 2026 ASCE.

title: MaskLenNet: A Query-Based Instance Segmentation and Length Prediction Network for Quantitative Industrial Tool Wear and Breakage Assessment
authors: Pan Y.; He K.; Yin C.; Zhang Y.; Luo Y.; Wang Y.
src: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
abstract: Tool wear detection is essential for machining quality control and predictive maintenance, but conventional inspection is often manual, time-consuming, and operator-dependent. Existing learning-based visual methods still face challenges in jointly achieving reliable wear-type recognition, accurate wear-region localization, and quantitative wear-width measurement under shop-floor imaging conditions. To address these issues, this study proposes MaskLenNet, a query-based instance segmentation and length prediction network for solid carbide end-milling tool diagnosis. MaskLenNet combines a Swin Transformer backbone, query-based instance-mask prediction, wear-oriented attention, and a key-point head that directly estimates the maximum wear-land width (VB). Evaluation uses 234 images from 54 physical tools under a tool-disjoint split, so different rotations of one tool cannot occur in both training and evaluation sets. On the held-out test set, MaskLenNet achieves 96.52% matched-instance classification accuracy, 95.75% foreground instance mIoU, and a VB mean absolute error of 0.010214 mm. Relative to BEiT-Base, the gains are 3.04 and 3.60 percentage points in accuracy and mIoU, respectively. title: An integrated image instance segmentation and multi-objective population balance framework for crystallization kinetics inversion
authors: Si N.; Yao T.; Wang S.; Xu R.; Gao Z.; Gong J.
abstract: The crystal size distribution is a critical quality attribute of crystalline products, yet extracting two-dimensional crystal size distributions from in situ microscopy images remains hindered by particle occlusion and computational cost. Here we couple instance segmentation with a two-dimensional population balance model to achieve kinetic parameter inversion from crystal images acquired at 100 frames per minute. The segmentation pipeline yields a mask mean average precision of 0.765 with an end-to-end throughput of 2.80 frames per second. The two-dimensional population balance model incorporates mixed primary–secondary nucleation and size-dependent anisotropic growth along both crystal axes. Seven kinetic parameters are simultaneously calibrated by minimizing the Hellinger distance between experimental and simulated major- and minor-axis crystal size distributions using multi-objective optimization. The best compromise solution achieves a combined Hellinger distance of 0.298. Over the entire crystallization window, primary nucleation contributes only a negligible initial seed population, and secondary nucleation generates virtually all crystals. The growth rate constant ratio of 2.0 yields an actual growth rate ratio of approximately 1.5 due to size-dependent decay. Bootstrap uncertainty quantification (30 replicates) indicates that secondary nucleation parameters are the most tightly constrained quantities. This end-to-end framework, from raw image acquisition to mechanistic kinetic inversion, provides a template for image-based crystallization kinetics analysis. © 2026 Chinese Society of Particuology and Institute of Process Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

abstract: As a key equipment in large-scale bridge construction, the deformation state of the main girder structure of the bridge erection machine during the girder erection process is directly related to construction safety. Traditional monitoring methods have limitations such as poor real-time performance and complex equipment layout. This paper proposes an innovative non-contact monitoring and early warning system based on image recognition and deep learning. By integrating technologies in the interdisciplinary field, intelligent perception of the safety state of the main girder of the bridge erection machine is realized. The core of the system lies in deploying specially designed targets at key positions of the main girder of the bridge erection machine, collecting image sequences using high-resolution industrial cameras, integrating the YOLOv5 target detection algorithm to achieve rapid target positioning, adopting the Mask R-CNN instance segmentation network to obtain pixel-level accurate target contours, performing image distortion correction with Zhang Zhengyou's calibration method, and finally converting pixel displacement into physical displacement through a displacement calculation model. The system can achieve a measurement accuracy of 1 pixel, which can meet the response and accuracy requirements for real-time monitoring in engineering sites. title: YOLOv8-SM-seg for screw hole localisation and vision-guided tracking in digital twin
authors: Chao Y.; Lu H.; Zhu H.; Tan C.; Dai G.
abstract: In intelligent assembly, screw holes localisation is susceptible to environmental disturbances and hardware limitations, leading to screw misalignment and increased development costs. To address this, an improved instance segmentation model, YOLOv8-SM-Seg, is proposed for precise screw hole localisation. A digital twin system integrating the robot operating system (ROS) with Unity is constructed to enable virtual debugging and cost reduction. YOLOv8-SM-Seg incorporates ShuffleNetV2 for model lightweighting and a multi-scale dilated attention (MSDA) module for enhanced robustness. A combined dataset is created from the WEEE screw disassembly dataset and a custom circuit board dataset. The proposed model achieves a mAP of 96.4%, improving upon YOLOv8-Seg while reducing parameters and computational cost by 30% and 22%, respectively. Compared with models from the past two years, including YOLOv11-Seg, YOLOv8-RFA, YOLOv8-duidie, and YOLOv8-lanslide, YOLOv8-SM-Seg achieves a competitive recall of 92.7%, only 0.2% lower than YOLOv8-duidie, but with 2.9% and 1.5% improvements in precision and mAP. It also outperforms YOLOv11-Seg in precision by 0.9% while maintaining a similar mAP. Screw hole localisation is mapped to world coordinates via YOLOv8-SM-Seg and homography calibration, and ArUco markers enable real-time pose tracking. The proposed approach demonstrates high accuracy and efficiency for digital twin-based intelligent assembly. © 2025 The Author(s). Published by Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

abstract: The integration of digital technologies in the shipbuilding industry has become essential to improve efficiency and ensure precision in complex manufacturing processes. This study explores the application of computer vision techniques for the identification and traceability of minor and simple subassemblies in shipbuilding. We developed a dual approach combining 3D point cloud analysis and 2D deep learning based instance segmentation to detect and classify components. A depth camera was used to acquire 3D point clouds and high-quality 2D images. For the 3D approach, we used surface and edge matching techniques, and for the 2D approach, we fine-tuned advanced instance segmentation models such as YOLO11 and MaskRCNN2. The results show that this combined approach significantly improves the reliability of subassembly identification, which is essential for improving traceability, reducing errors, and optimizing production workflows in the shipbuilding sector. © 2026, College Publications. title: AIS-HCSR: A hierarchical cross-source point cloud registration method with adaptive instance segmentation; [基于自适应实例分割的层级化跨源点云配准方法]
authors: Zhang M.; Wang M.; Han Y.; Ma N.
src: Gongcheng Kexue Xuebao/Chinese Journal of Engineering
abstract: Cross-source point cloud registration is a key technique for multisensor fusion in mobile robotics and intelligent perception, where point clouds acquired from heterogeneous modalities (e.g., LiDAR, depth cameras, and structure-from-motion reconstructions) must be aligned into a unified coordinate system to support reliable pose estimation and 3D scene understanding. In practical indoor and industrial environments, cross-source registration remains challenging owing to large differences in sampling density and spatial distribution, distinct noise patterns, limited field-of-view overlap, and the frequent presence of repeated structures or multiple similar objects. These factors make correspondence search highly ambiguous and cause existing optimization-based pipelines or learning-based methods to struggle in simultaneously achieving global consistency and high local accuracy, particularly in complex multi-object scenes. To address these issues, this paper proposes adaptive instance segmentation hierarchical cross-source registration (AIS-HCSR), a hierarchical cross-source point cloud registration method based on adaptive instance segmentation, which performs progressive registration from the scene level to the object level and finally to the point cloud level. At the scene level, an adaptive geometric feature encoding scheme is designed. This scheme jointly models pairwise distance relations and triplet angle relations and dynamically reweights the two types of geometric embeddings according to local geometric complexity. The resulting geometric structural embedding is injected into a transformer-based geometric perception network to compute the self- and cross-attention to enable robust feature extraction and initial matching across modalities. Based on the optimized correlation matrix, the top-ranked correspondences are selected to estimate an initial rigid transformation, providing a globally consistent prior for subsequent refinement. At the object level, a density-aware adaptive Euclidean clustering algorithm is introduced to segment each point cloud into instances with explicit physical meaning. An instance correspondence mechanism is then constructed by propagating superpoint matches to instance pairs, computing matching frequency and fusing it with centroid-based positional similarity to form an instance similarity matrix. The optimal instance associations are obtained by solving a bipartite matching problem. To further suppress ambiguities caused by multiple similar objects and improve robustness under imperfect clustering (e.g., over-segmentation or under-segmentation in contact scenarios), a spatial layout consistency verification strategy is proposed. The strategy evaluates triangle-based configurations of instances and filters out instance correspondences that violate global spatial relations to prevent incorrect matches from propagating to later optimization. At the point cloud level, for each matched instance pair, point-to-plane residual minimization is performed to obtain a locally refined transformation with improved convergence under cross-source density gaps. The set of local transformations is then integrated through a global least-squares formulation and solved efficiently to yield a single final transformation, achieving fine registration while preserving global consistency across instances. Experiments on the 3DCSR dataset (including LiDAR-Kinect and Kinect-SfM modality pairs) demonstrate that AIS-HCSR achieves a recall of 81.19%, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art FF-LOGO by 5.45 percentage points, with translation and rotation errors of 0.08 m and 2.42°, respectively. The average end-to-end runtime is 1.33 s per point cloud pair. Ablation studies further verify that the scene-level registration and object-level matching with local-to-global optimization are complementary and jointly contribute to the performance gain. Overall, AIS-HCSR improves registration robustness in low-overlap and large density-difference settings by explicitly combining scene-scale structural priors with instance-scale geometric constraints to provide an effective solution for cross-source point cloud registration in complex multi-object environments. © 2026 Science Press. title: DPR-GAN: Generative Network for Powder Spreading Defect Image Based on Defect Perception and Reconstruction; [DPR-GAN:一 种 基 于 缺 陷 感 知 与 重 建 的 铺 粉 缺 陷图 像 生 成 网 络]
authors: Quanmin G.; Yikang Z.; Chenxiao L.; Chengxing L.; Jiongya H.
abstract: Objective In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing, the quality of powder spreading directly affects the forming quality of structural part printed. So, it’s essential to monitor the defects in the powder spreading process. However, in practice, the probability of powder spreading defects is extremely low, resulting in a scarcity, an imbalance in categories, and a poor diversity of defect samples, which seriously affects the generalization ability of existing detection algorithms. It is an effective solution to generate the defect samples conforming to the real shape by data augmentation. The traditional methods such as geometric transformation are simple and easy to implement, but they lack the ability to simulate defect morphology and have poor augmentation effects on complex defects. Generative adversarial network (GAN) can generate relatively realistic defect images, but it cannot focus on the defect areas, so the conditional GAN (CGAN) is often used to impose constraints on the generated defect categories. However, when the proportion of defect area is relatively small in the label image, the defect generation effect is poor and the generated category is single. The image translation-based GAN can generate images containing specific categories of defects through defect semantic labels, and the defect styles are not constrained by fixed patterns. However, it does not focus on the generation of defect areas, resulting in a relatively low quality of defect generation. The overall generation quality of the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM)-based network is relatively high, with distinct boundaries of defect areas. However, it pays insufficient attention to the generation of defect details and has high requirements for computing resources. Therefore, this paper proposes a defect perception and reconstruction based generative adversarial network (DPR-GAN). Methods First, this paper introduces a spectral normalization layer into the discriminator of the image translation-based BicycleGAN. By applying Lipschitz constraint to the weight matrix, the maximum amplitude of the gradient change of the discriminator is limited, thereby suppressing the large amplitude oscillation phenomenon of the loss function during the training process, and thus improving the stability of the generated quality of the defect image. Second, we introduce the efficient channel attention (ECA) into the generator. By establishing the dependency relationship between channels through the local interaction of convolutional kernels, the weight values of different feature channels can be adaptively adjusted to increase the weight of channels related to defects. This can enhance the perception ability of the generation network for defect features, prompting the generator to focus on generating defect areas with high information density and relatively complex features. Finally, we add the defect reconstruction loss to the total loss function. By constricting the L1 loss and the structural similarity (SSIM) loss of the defect area, the sensitivity of the network to the pixel differences of the defect area is enhanced, and the detail consistency of the generated defects is strengthened in visual perception. This avoids the problem of defect optimization being diluted due to background-dominated loss calculation. Results and Discussions The comparative experiments with five advanced image translation networks show that the DPR-GAN proposed in this paper is significantly superior to the comparative networks in terms of the quality and detail representation of the generated powder spreading defect images. The average PSNR of various types of the defect images generated by DPR-GAN reaches 32.147 dB, and the average SSIM reaches 0.809, which are respectively increased by an average of 4.337 dB and 0.036 compared with the BicycleGAN (Table 1). The powder spreading defects generated by the proposed network have the advantages of distinct features, true details and clear edges. The generated background area is more delicate, and the transition of gray values between the background and the defects is natural (Fig. 8). The ablation experiment results show that by introducing spectral normalization, ECA and defect reconstruction loss, the average PSNR and SSIM of the generated images of DPR-GAN are improved (Table 2). Moreover, the distortion phenomenon is eliminated, the defect area is more prominent, and the defect details are clearer (Fig. 9). Finally, the experiments on the applicability of enhanced datasets show that the expanded dataset by the proposed network performs well in the defect detection and instance segmentation tasks of Mask-RCNN and YOLACT networks. The mean average precision at intersection-over-union ratio of 0.5 (mAP@0.5) of detection of the two networks has increased by 2.92 percentage points and 2.68 percentage points respectively compared with the expanded dataset of the traditional method. The mAP@0.5 of segmentation has increased by 3.26 percentage points and 2.10 percentage points, respectively (Tables 3 and 4). This indicates that the diverse and high-quality defect images generated by DPR-GAN can improve the accuracy and generalization ability of the defect detection segmentation model. Conclusions The DPR-GAN proposed in this paper realizes the generation of powder spreading defect images with controllable regions and categories according to the defect semantic label images. By introducing a spectral normalization layer into the discriminator, the stability of the generated quality of defect images has been effectively improved. The introduction of ECA in the generator enhances the perception of defect features by the generation network. The construction of defect area reconstruction loss has improved the generation quality of defect details. The experimental results show that the DPR-GAN is significantly superior to the contrast networks in terms of the quality, detail and visual consistency of the generated defect images. The defect images generated by the DPR-GAN can provide high-quality and diversified data support for the subsequent powder spreading defect detection and instance segmentation tasks. In addition, the DPR-GAN is also applicable to other scenarios that require diversified and high-quality data expansion, such as industrial defect detection, medical image analysis, and other fields. © 2026 Chinese Laser Press. title: Design and Development of a Vision-Guided Automated Chinese Yam Seedling Planter
authors: Shi T.; Li T.; Tang Y.; Zhan S.; Feng S.; Lu P.; Hong X.
abstract: Chinese yam planting requires horizontal placement, consistent apical–basal orientation, controlled spacing, and low-damage handling of slender seed segments. This study developed and field-evaluated an integrated vision-guided Chinese yam planter combining furrow opening, feeding, visual inspection and rejection, orientation adjustment, buffered discharge, spacing regulation, furrow tracking, seed placement, and soil covering. Conventional image processing extracted seed-segment length and end orientation, an EfficientNet-B0–kNN one-class method supported auxiliary visual-anomaly screening, and a YOLO11s-seg model with PID control-enabled furrow tracking. Field tests and a two-factor experiment were conducted under sandy-soil conditions. The prototype achieved 22 seedlings min−1, a spacing coefficient of variation of 8.4%, a miss-seeding rate of 4.5 ± 1.3%, an orientation accuracy of 99%, and a path-tracking RMSE of 2.30 ± 0.18 cm; forward velocity was the dominant factor affecting spacing uniformity. The screening module achieved a 98.6% interception rate on marker-simulated anomalies under controlled imaging conditions, while recognition of natural defects remains unvalidated. The system can reduce reliance on skilled labor, and its modular structure and quantified performance provide practical references for users and equipment manufacturers. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Foundation model cascades enable zero-shot microscopy image analysis for cell therapy manufacturing
authors: Chen R.Q.; Lee Y.; Joffe B.; Serafini C.E.; Casteleiro Costa P.; Wang B.; Kanwar B.; Balakirsky S.; Silva Trenkle A.D.; Kippner L.E.; LeCompte I.; Li Y.; Brown C.E.; Kwong G.A.; Robles F.E.; Roy K.; Li J.
abstract: Background aims: The scalable manufacturing of cell therapies creates a significant need for robust process analytical technologies, where automated analysis of noninvasive microscopy images offers a powerful method for monitoring critical quality attributes. However, conventional machine-learning models are often bottlenecked by extensive data labeling and poor generalizability across different batch effects. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a foundational model cascade for the zero-shot analysis of microscopy images. Methods: In the first stage, a multimodal large language model (LLM) detects anomalies, and anomalous images immediately trigger an alert. Otherwise, the segment anything model performs exhaustive instance segmentation, and the detected objects are classified by the LLM to estimate cell counts and viability. Results: This unified, zero-shot approach delivers robust anomaly detection together with quantitative measures of cell count and health, without any task-specific fine-tuning. Conclusions: By combining pre-trained foundation models in a complementary cascade, our method provides a generalizable solution for real-time process monitoring and feedback control, paving the way for more scalable and automated cell therapy manufacturing. © 2026 International Society for Cellular Therapy

title: Fully automated method for parametric modelling of industrial facility elements
authors: Jayasinghe H.; Wang M.; Brilakis I.
abstract: Downstream applications of infrastructure models are highly reliant on accurate recovery of geometrical parameters of elements, especially in industrial facilities. However, current segmentation methods produce either point clusters, meshes or library templates as outputs, ignoring underlying geometry. This paper introduces an automated method for extracting geometrical parameters from output point clusters of instance segmentation methods. The paper proposes a two-stage pipeline consisting of regression of geometric parameters from point clusters, followed by iterative optimisation. This paper demonstrates that a robust objective function for measuring deviation between input and reconstructed models is critical for optimising geometries. The proposed solution is robust to noise and occlusions, and outperforms existing methods on primitive geometries, achieving around 30% reduction in chamfer and parameter errors in occluded scans compared to RANSAC. Crucially, it generalises to arbitrary parametric shapes, enabling modelling of non-primitive geometries. The method directly supports scan-to-BIM workflows by enabling reliable, parameter-consistent geometric modelling. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: An Improved Single-Stage Object Detection Model and Its Application to Oil Seal Defect Detection
authors: Chen Y.; Wu Y.; Wu X.; He W.; He G.; Cai X.
abstract: Oil seals, as core industrial components, often exhibit defects with sparse features and low contrast, posing significant challenges for traditional vision-based inspection methods. Although deep learning facilitates automatic feature extraction for defect detection, many instance segmentation models are computationally expensive, hindering their deployment in real-time edge applications. In this paper, we present an efficient oil seal defect detection model based on an enhanced YOLOv11n architecture (YOLOv11n_CDK). The proposed approach introduces several dynamic convolution variants and integrates the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) into the backbone. A newly designed parallel module, the nested asynchronous pooling convolutional module (NAPConv), is also incorporated to form a lightweight yet powerful feature extraction network. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline YOLOv11n, our model reduces computational cost by 4.76% and increases mAP@0.5 by 2.14%. When deployed on a Jetson Nano embedded device, the model achieves an average processing time of 6.3 ms per image, corresponding to a frame rate of 105–110 FPS. These outcomes highlight the model’s strong potential for high-performance, real-time industrial deployment, effectively balancing detection accuracy with low computational complexity. © 2025 by the authors.

title: Depth-guided multi-modal early optimization for 6D pose estimation
authors: Li Y.; Lyu E.
abstract: Zero-shot 6D object pose estimation typically follows a two-stage pipeline consisting of instance segmentation and pose estimation. However, segmentation errors in the first stage can propagate to the observed point cloud and degrade downstream registration, especially in low-texture, cluttered, or poorly illuminated scenes where RGB-only segmentation is often unstable. Directly applying SAM to raw depth maps is also insufficient, since the resulting masks are often unstable and do not provide reliable geometric proposals for downstream pose recovery. We propose DG-M2EO (Depth-Guided Multi-Modal Early Optimization), a training-free RGB-D front-end framework that operates under frozen pre-trained models and introduces depth-guided proposal generation into zero-shot 6D pose estimation. The framework incorporates a dedicated depth branch based on SAM, together with inverse-depth normalization, geometric consistency restoration, and geometry-aware mask filtering, so that depth-derived masks can serve as reliable instance proposals for downstream pose recovery. It further includes a multi-modal matching and scoring module with an Early-Optimization (EO) rule to reduce unnecessary computation when the depth proposal is already sufficiently reliable. Experiments on four BOP19 datasets (T-LESS, TUD-L, YCB-V, and LM-O) show that DG-M2EO is particularly beneficial on industrial datasets with weak texture and limited RGB discriminability, while remaining comparable on YCB-V. Compared with SAM6D under the same PEM backend, DG-M2EO improves the Mean4 BOP19 Average Recall from 74.1 to 76.1, corresponding to an overall gain of 2.0 points, with performance changes of + 6.3, +2.71, +0.6, and −1.6 on T-LESS, TUD-L, YCB-V, and LM-O, respectively. At the same time, the results on LM-O indicate that the benefit of the depth branch depends on scene geometry quality and may decrease under severe occlusion, clutter, or degraded depth observations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: DO-Net: An occlusion-discriminative decoupling neural network for estimating particle size distributions
authors: Cheng C.; Liang H.; Chen D.; Yan B.; Guo H.
abstract: In industries such as mineral processing and metallurgy, real-time and accurate monitoring of the particle size distribution (PSD) of bulk materials is of paramount importance. However, existing vision-based estimation methods are often hampered by densely stacked particles and severe occlusions, which tend to misclassify occluded fragments as intact small particles, thereby introducing systematic measurement bias and distorting the final PSD results. To address this issue, we propose a novel Decoupled Occlusion-Discrimination Network (DO-Net), which equips the particle segmentation task with explicit “occlusion discrimination” capability. DO-Net adopts a parallel dual-decoder architecture that effectively avoids optimization conflicts between the instance segmentation and occlusion discrimination tasks. We further propose the Pyramid Semantic-Gated Fusion (PSGF) module which exploits explicit semantic signals for cross-task guidance, and introduce a Lightweight Boundary Refiner (LBR) for high-fidelity segmentation masks. By segmenting the particles and proactively discarding invalid measurements from the occluded particles, the proposed method achieves unbiased PSD statistics. Experimental results demonstrate that DO-Net improves particle segmentation performance on the benchmark dataset by 1.7% over the strongest baseline model; more importantly, it corrects systematic measurement bias, raising the correlation coefficient between predicted and ground-truth PSDs to 0.9505. Our work provides a robust and effective solution for unbiased particle size estimation in complex industrial scenarios. The code and dataset of this paper have been made publicly available at https://github.com/Mr-ERO/DONet . © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Strip tobacco size ratio estimation via multiscale feature fusion segmentation and area-mass fitting under transmittance imaging

abstract: In the process of shredding cigarettes, the proportion of large and medium cigarette leaf fragments is a key quality indicator, which directly affects the uniformity and production efficiency of shredding. Traditional screening and area-based methods have the problems of low efficiency, poor real-Time and limited adaptability to complex tobacco leaf structures. In order to solve these limitations, this paper proposes a real-Time online detection method that integrates the segmentation of tobacco leaf instances, size classification and the estimation of the proportion of large and medium pieces. Our method builds a multi-Type tobacco leaf data set and develops an enhanced segmentation network based on YOLO11. By introducing an improved channel attention mechanism, it can better capture weak textures and overlapping areas. A calibrated area-mass regression model has also been established to achieve an accurate estimate of tobacco leaf mass. Experiments show that the proposed method is superior to the comparative model in terms of standard indicators and maintains strong robustness in complex scenarios. The regression model has also achieved high accuracy, providing reliable support for proportional calculation. Overall, this method has significantly improved accuracy, robustness and real-Time performance. Our research provides practical solutions for the quality monitoring and process control of industrial tobacco leafing and re-roasting production lines. © COPYRIGHT SPIE.

title: Deep Learning-Based Toolkit Inspection: Object Detection and Segmentation in Assembly Lines
authors: Mukundan A.; Karmakar R.; Gupta D.; Wang H.-C.
abstract: Modern manufacturing processes have become more reliant on automation because of the accelerated transition from Industry 3.0 to Industry 4.0. Manual inspection of products on assembly lines remains inefficient, prone to errors and lacks consistency, emphasizing the need for a reliable and automated inspection system. Leveraging both object detection and image segmentation approaches, this research proposes a vision-based solution for the detection of various kinds of tools in the toolkit using deep learning (DL) models. Two Intel RealSense D455f depth cameras were arranged in a top down configuration to capture both RGB and depth images of the toolkits. After applying multiple constraints and enhancing them through preprocessing and augmentation, a dataset consisting of 3300 annotated RGB-D photos was generated. Several DL models were selected through a comprehensive assessment of mean Average Precision (mAP), precision-recall equilibrium, inference latency (target ≥30 FPS), and computational burden, resulting in a preference for YOLO and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks (R-CNN) variants over ViT-based models due to the latter’s increased latency and resource requirements. YOLOV5, YOLOV8, YOLOV11, Faster R-CNN, and Mask R-CNN were trained on the annotated dataset and evaluated using key performance metrics (Recall, Accuracy, F1-score, and Precision). YOLOV11 demonstrated balanced excellence with 93.0% precision, 89.9% recall, and a 90.6% F1-score in object detection, as well as 96.9% precision, 95.3% recall, and a 96.5% F1-score in instance segmentation with an average inference time of 25 ms per frame (≈40 FPS), demonstrating real-time performance. Leveraging these results, a YOLOV11-based windows application was successfully deployed in a real-time assembly line environment, where it accurately processed live video streams to detect and segment tools within toolkits, demonstrating its practical effectiveness in industrial automation. The application is capable of precisely measuring socket dimensions by utilising edge detection techniques on YOLOv11 segmentation masks, in addition to detection and segmentation. This makes it possible to do specification-level quality control right on the assembly line, which improves the ability to examine things in real time. The implementation is a big step forward for intelligent manufacturing in the Industry 4.0 paradigm. It provides a scalable, efficient, and accurate way to do automated inspection and dimensional verification activities. Copyright © 2025 The Authors.

title: Vision-Based Instance Segmentation of Piezoelectric Crystal Defects Using a Hybrid Bidirectional CNN–Transformer Network
authors: Hou Z.; He Z.; Huang H.; Chen X.
abstract: Accurate defect instance segmentation is essential for automated quality inspection of piezoelectric crystals, where scratches, stains, and other surface defects often show large scale variation, irregular morphology, and weak contrast against complex backgrounds. Existing CNN-based segmentation models capture local texture effectively but are limited in global context modeling, whereas Transformer-based models often require stronger local detail preservation for fine industrial defects. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid bidirectional bridging CNN–Transformer network, named HBCTNet, for piezoelectric crystal defect instance segmentation. HBCTNet introduces a Convolution-Transformer Bidirectional Bridging Block (CTB) that enables lightweight two-way interaction between convolutional local features and Transformer global representations. A Frequency and Spatial Convolution (FSC) module is designed to enhance defect-related details in both spatial and frequency domains, and a Multi-Scale Feature Pyramid Network (MS-FPN) fuses features across scales. On the reported image partition of the self-constructed dataset, HBCTNet-S obtains 92.3% box AP and 89.9% mask AP with 12.67 M parameters and 48.1 G FLOPs. Its mask AP is 2.1 percentage points higher than YOLO11-SEG and 2.4 percentage points higher than YOLOv9-SEG under the reported comparison. These results support the effectiveness of the architecture within the evaluated dataset; inference speed and cross-domain generalization remain to be assessed. © 2026 by the authors.

title: A vision-based safety system for human–robot collaboration using a real-time digital twin in RoboDK
authors: Dosymzhan B.; Esimzhan A.; Ainur A.; Qasobov G.; Ilyas M.
src: Journal of Mechanical Science and Technology
abstract: This work presents a low-cost, vision-based safety monitoring system for human–robot collaboration (HRC) in industrial environments. A power-bank assembly case study involving two robots and a human operator is used for validation. One robot performs pick-and-place operations, while the second robot executes screwing tasks, and a human assistant performs soldering. Human presence is detected using a YOLOv8 instance-segmentation model with a single overhead RGB camera. Based on the detected human position, the workspace is divided into three adaptive safety zones: red, yellow, and green. The red zone is derived from the robot’s reachable workspace in RoboDK and triggers a functional stop when a human enters the hazardous region. The yellow zone reduces robot speed by 50 %, while the green zone allows full operation. A RoboDK digital twin is used for real-time monitoring of robot motion, enabling additional collision awareness during operation. Experimental results using real robotic systems demonstrate that integrating lightweight vision-based detection with digital-twin monitoring provides an effective and scalable approach for improving safety awareness in collaborative robotic work cells. © The Korean Society of Mechanical Engineers and Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Instance-aware vision-guided robotic sorting of metal waste using W²G-Net
authors: Hao Z.; Wang Y.; Wang X.
abstract: Purpose – This study aims to develop a robust vision-guided framework for instance-level recognition and grasp-based classification of metal waste in dense, multi-scale and highly reflective industrial environments, addressing the challenges of clutter, mild occlusion and dynamic operation conditions commonly encountered during the post-preprocessing sorting stage of automated recycling systems. Design/methodology/approach – A lightweight two-stage What & Where to Grasp framework, termed W²G-Net, is presented. The framework adopts a cascaded pipeline integrating an optimized YOLOv11-Seg for instance-level perception and an improved Generative Residual Convolutional Neural Network (GRCNN) for planar grasp planning. An instance-mask-constrained grasp feasibility modeling method is introduced to enforce geometric and interference constraints, together with a time-compensated dynamic grasp model for conveyor belt scenarios. The approach is evaluated on metal waste segmentation data sets, a newly constructed metal waste 2D grasp data set, and the Cornell grasp data set. Findings – Experimental results show that the optimized YOLOv11-Seg achieves a 17.1% inference speed improvement, while the enhanced GRCNN increases inference speed by 59.5%. The proposed two-stage framework operates at 16.2 frames per second (FPS) for single-target and 8.6 FPS for multi-target scenarios, with recognition accuracy and grasp success rates exceeding 90%. Grasp stability is significantly improved in cluttered and dynamic metal-waste environments. Originality/value – This work presents a two-stage grasping framework that combines instance-level segmentation, planar grasp planning and time-compensated dynamic grasp modeling, providing an efficient, scalable and industrially applicable solution for automated metal waste sorting. © 2026 Emerald Publishing Limited

title: Automatic detection, segmentation, and characterization of 3-nitro-1,2,4-triazol-5-one (NTO) crystal particles during cooling crystallization using deep learning

title: Edge Self-Attention-supported instance segmentation and quality inspectionin virtual trial assembly
authors: Wei Z.; Liu Z.; Zhang L.; Li J.; Zhang Y.
abstract: To address assembly challenges in bolted prefabricated steel structures, this study proposes an automated framework that integrates an Edge Self-Attention (ESA) segmentation model with a Virtual Trial Assembly (VTA) pipeline using multi-source point clouds. By leveraging precomputed normal vectors, the ESA model captures subtle cylindrical features and mitigates the severe class imbalance inherent in industrial point clouds. The integrated VTA pipeline automates centroid localization, hole-group matching, and assembly error evaluation. Validation using blueprint-derived and LiDAR-scanned point clouds from a real bridge project shows that the proposed model achieves semantic and instance segmentation mIoUs above 0.98, while the VTA pipeline provides sub-millimeter-level alignment-error assessment in multi-component scenarios. This framework supports automated virtual assembly and quantitative quality assessment, reducing the risk of on-site assembly mismatch and rework. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Real-Time Spatiotemporal Prediction of Flow-Front Evolution in Vacuum-Assisted Resin Infusion via ConvLSTM
authors: Li Y.; Xu Z.; Ye W.; Li Y.; Li Z.
abstract: Real-time flow-front tracking in vacuum-assisted resin infusion (VARI) is critical for mitigating composite manufacturing defects. However, traditional numerical solvers suffer from prohibitive computational latency. This study presents a deep learning-based spatiotemporal framework for faster-than-real-time flow-front prediction. Training datasets are generated via a parallelized control-volume finite element method (CVFEM) integrated with Karhunen-Loève (KL) expansions to capture stochastic preform permeability fields. A Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) network is developed to autoregressively predict two-dimensional transient fluid advancement while strictly preserving spatial topologies. To evaluate industrial deployment, an in situ visual-predictive closed loop is established by deploying a YOLOv11-seg instance segmentation model on real manufacturing video feeds. Results demonstrate that the integrated network executes a 10-step future spatiotemporal rollout within single-digit millisecond computational latency, maintaining an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 95.33% at Step 10 on physical experimental data. This paradigm provides a robust data-driven strategy for proactive quality control and online digital-twin implementations in liquid composite molding. © 2026 Society of Plastics Engineers.

abstract: This paper presents a multi-view RGB dataset and supervised deep learning baselines for footwear damage detection in industrial remanufacturing. The original 10-class defect taxonomy was grouped into three remanufacturing-oriented categories: Detached Sole (DS), Non-repairable (NR), and Repairable (R), to reduce label imbalance while preserving decision relevance. title: Critical Review of Recent Advances in AI-Enhanced SEM and EDS Techniques for Metallic Microstructure Characterization
authors: Abdelal G.; Chan C.-W.; McLoone S.
abstract: This critical review explores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and computer vision (CV), on scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) for metallic microstructure analysis, spanning research from 2010 to 2025. It critically evaluates how AI techniques balance automation, accuracy, and scalability, analysing why certain methods (e.g., Vision Transformers for complex microstructures) excel in specific contexts and how trade-offs in data availability, computational resources, and interpretability shape their adoption. The review examines AI-driven techniques, including semantic segmentation, object detection, and instance segmentation, which automate the identification and characterisation of microstructural features, defects, and inclusions, achieving enhanced accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility compared to traditional manual methods. It introduces the Microstructure Analysis Spectrum, a novel framework categorising techniques by task complexity and scalability, providing a new lens to understand AI’s role in materials science. The paper also evaluates AI’s role in chemical composition analysis and predictive modelling, facilitating rapid forecasts of mechanical properties such as hardness and fracture strain. Practical applications in steelmaking (e.g., automated inclusion characterisation) and case studies on high-entropy alloys and additively manufactured metals underscore AI’s benefits, including reduced analysis time and improved quality control. Extending prior reviews, this work incorporates recent advancements like Vision Transformers, 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Key challenges—data scarcity, model interpretability, and computational demands—are critically analysed, with representative trade-offs from the literature highlighted (e.g., GANs can substantially augment effective dataset size through synthetic data generation, typically at the cost of significantly increased training time). © 2026 by the authors.

title: An efficient and lightweight network for detecting bulk material conveyor belts
authors: Luo J.; Mao C.; Wang Y.; Yao Z.; Cui Z.
abstract: In complex and dynamic industrial environments, conveyor belt deviation poses a serious threat to system stability and production safety. Therefore, developing a real-time and accurate belt deviation detection method is crucial to ensure the efficient and safe operation of the system. Traditional vision-based detection methods often suffer from poor robustness under strong interference conditions such as dust, fog, and uneven lighting, making them unsuitable for on-site applications. Although deep learning-based detection methods offer superior performance, challenges remain in terms of hardware deployment, inference speed, and stability under complex disturbances. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient instance segmentation network designed specifically for conveyor belt detection (EBSnet). Based on a channel shuffle mechanism, the network incorporates a highly efficient and lightweight backbone and neck architecture. Considering the large-scale and single-target characteristics of conveyor belts, a single-scale segmentation head is introduced to enhance target adaptability and detection efficiency. Furthermore, a structured pruning strategy is applied to compress the network, significantly reducing parameter count and computational cost while maintaining detection accuracy, thus improving its deployment performance on edge computing devices. To enhance the ability of the model to perceive belt edge contours, an edge-aware loss function is introduced, effectively improving segmentation accuracy in boundary regions. Experiments conducted on the embedded platform NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX demonstrate that the EBSnet model requires only 4.6 GFLOPs and 1.052M parameters, achieving an AP@0.5 of 0.9913 on a custom industrial conveyor belt dataset. It also reaches inference speeds of 30 FPS and 21 FPS under single-stream and three-stream video inputs, respectively. These results validate that the proposed algorithm achieves high accuracy, low latency, and strong robustness in conveyor belt deviation monitoring under limited computational resources. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2025.
