title: A novel point cloud and attribute adjacency graph integrated machining feature recognition approach
authors: Yao J.; Liang X.; Liu J.; Wang Z.
abstract: Machining feature recognition (MFR) is the process of inferring manufacturing semantics from the geometric information of Computer-Aided Design models. It is a key task for enabling data exchange among Computer-Aided Design, Computer-Aided Process Planning and Computer-Aided Engineering system, and plays a crucial role in digital intelligent manufacturing. Complex mechanical parts models often exhibit intricate topological relationships and multiple intersecting features, making traditional rule-based feature recognition methods inadequate for handling such complexities. This challenge has driven the development of deep learning-based approaches. However, existing deep learning methods struggle to fully represent and utilize Boundary Representation (B-rep) model information. For instance, point cloud-based methods ignore the topological information of B-rep models, while graph-based methods cannot effectively represent the geometric shape of models. To address these challenges, we propose a B-rep model representation that integrates point cloud information and attribute adjacency graph to effectively express both geometric and topological information. Additionally, to recognize machining features and their associated surfaces, we introduce a multi-task graph neural network for semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and bottom face segmentation. At last, the proposed method is evaluated on the several datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively represents the geometric and topological information of B-rep models and enables accurate machining feature recognition and semantic information prediction using a graph neural network. title: Surface defect detection in silicon rod using machine vision
authors: Zhao S.; He H.; Hong W.; Guo Y.
src: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: As a core raw material in semiconductor manufacturing, surface defects on square silicon rods—such as line marks, watermarks, chipped edges, grinding wheel marks, and scratches—directly impact the performance and reliability of downstream devices. Therefore, achieving efficient and precise defect detection is crucial for ensuring product quality. To address the challenges in detecting typical defects on all four sides of square silicon rods, this paper builds upon the existing instance segmentation model Mask R-CNN by introducing a cascade structure to enhance its performance. Cascade Mask R-CNN enhances candidate box quality and defect localization accuracy progressively through sequentially optimizing the classification and regression processes of detection heads. During training, losses are computed separately for classification and regression tasks at each cascade stage, enabling end-to-end joint optimization. Comparisons between the improved model and the original model on a self-built silicon rod dataset demonstrate that Cascade Mask R-CNN achieves an 11.7% improvement in mAP_50. Furthermore, for small-sized defects commonly found on silicon rod surfaces, Cascade Mask R-CNN shows significantly enhanced detection performance, achieving a 10.1% improvement in mAP_s compared to the original model. This study validates the feasibility of Cascade Mask R-CNN for detecting surface defects on square silicon rods, providing a reference for algorithm design in industrial silicon rod visual inspection systems. © 2026 SPIE.

title: CAD-guided editable 3D Gaussian reconstruction framework for industrial assembly preview
authors: Wang Y.; Zhang C.; Pang J.; Zheng P.
abstract: Interactive high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction can reflect actual scene changes and preview the outcomes of operational actions, thereby enabling robot applications under frequently varying conditions such as embodied intelligence and human–robot collaboration. It is of significant engineering value for enhancing the resilience of intelligent manufacturing systems and accelerating the transition of manufacturing paradigms toward Industry 5.0. However, long static-reconstruction runtime and limited editability impede its use in dynamic industrial assembly. This paper proposes a computer-aided design (CAD)-guided editable 3D Gaussian reconstruction framework for industrial assembly preview. A feature-based structure-from-motion (SfM) initialization constructs sparse point clouds under weak textures and reflections. Instance segmentation and mask-based filtering generate independent part-level Gaussians, while CAD priors guide alignment, local editing, and staged assembly. Experiments show that Preview(Ours) reduces Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) by 58.0% and improves Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM)-Gray/SSIM-RGB by 33.2%/31.1% over CAD-only, while outperforming multi-view stereo (MVS) and Instant Neural Graphics Primitives (Instant-NGP) with 11 min post-SfM time. Local updates take 1.216–1.321 s without retraining, and CAD deviation tests show stable registration under mild perturbations. Thus, the framework enables CAD-consistent, editable high-fidelity assembly preview for interactive manufacturing scenes. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Synthetic Data for Data-Efficient Agricultural Computer Vision: Three Datasets and a Multi-Task Benchmark Across Real and Simulated Domains
authors: Moonen S.; Jansen W.; Liao W.; Rahmani M.H.; Ahar A.; Bey-Temsamani A.; Steckel J.; Michiels N.
abstract: The availability of large annotated datasets remains a major bottleneck for deploying computer vision systems in agricultural and agri-food applications, particularly for tasks requiring fine-grained annotations such as defect detection and instance segmentation. Synthetic data generation offers a scalable alternative, but its effectiveness in complex real-world scenarios remains insufficiently understood. In this work, the role of synthetic data is investigated across three representative tasks each posing unique challenges: apple detection in orchard environments, potato–stone classification in industrial sorting, and carrot crack detection for quality inspection. The real and synthetic data, as well as their annotations, are publicly available. The synthetic data is created using a set of tools for fast large-scale procedural scene generation with highly detailed natural assets. For each task, datasets are constructed combining real and synthetically generated images with pixel-level annotations. Training strategies are systematically evaluated using fully real, limited real, synthetic-only, and combined datasets. The results show that synthetic-only training leads to a clear performance gap on real-world data, with mAP50 decreasing from 0.866–0.891 for fully real training to 0.396–0.703 for synthetic-only training across the three use cases. However, combining synthetic data with only 10 real images recovers 75–98% of the gap between training on those 10 real images alone (mAP50 0.194–0.497) and full real training, reaching mAP50 values of 0.723–0.885. These findings highlight the potential of synthetic data for improving data efficiency and provide a reproducible benchmark for future research on sim-to-real transfer in agricultural computer vision. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Few-Shot Pose Estimation for Robotic Sorting of Flexible Packages with Complex Overlapping and Ambiguous Boundaries
authors: Wang J.; Zhang J.; Jiang L.; Kong S.; Lin X.; Zhou X.; Yan W.; Wu H.
src: IEEE International Conference on Control and Automation, ICCA
abstract: In industrial logistics environments, chaotically stacked flexible packages present substantial challenges for robotic sorting due to severe overlap, ambiguous object boundaries, and large morphological variations. These issues are further amplified in few-shot scenarios, where limited training data often leads to overfitting and poor generalization in conventional vision models. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a few-shot pose estimation framework for robotic sorting of flexible packages with complex overlapping and boundary ambiguity. First, to alleviate data scarcity, a generative data augmentation strategy is developed by combining explicit physical spatial transformations with implicit feature disentanglement using a β-VAE. This hybrid augmentation mechanism significantly improves the diversity and robustness of the training dataset under severe occlusion conditions. Second, a multi-task perception network based on Directional Mask R-CNN is introduced to simultaneously perform instance segmentation and orientation estimation, enabling accurate perception of overlapping flexible packages. The 3D spatial centroid (X, Y, Z) of each target is then efficiently recovered by aligning the predicted masks with depth data, enabling reliable pose estimation for robotic manipulation. Finally, a systemlevel validation platform is implemented using a FRANKA robotic arm equipped with a vacuum suction gripper to execute autonomous sorting tasks. Experiments in real chaotic stacking scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a visual recognition accuracy of 99.7% and a physical grasping success rate of 86.5%, validating its effectiveness for few-shot robotic sorting of flexible packages. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Prompt-Driven Lightweight Foundation Model for Instance Segmentation-Based Fault Detection in Freight Trains
authors: Sun G.; Liang Q.; Pan X.; Liu M.; Zhang Y.
src: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Accurate visual fault detection in freight trains remains a critical challenge for intelligent transportation system maintenance, due to complex operational environments, structurally repetitive components, and frequent occlusions or contaminations in safety-critical regions. Conventional instance segmentation methods based on convolutional neural networks and Transformers often suffer from poor generalization and limited boundary accuracy under such conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight self-prompted instance segmentation framework tailored for freight train fault detection. Our method leverages the Segment Anything Model by introducing a self-prompt generation module that automatically produces task-specific prompts, enabling effective knowledge transfer from foundation models to domain-specific inspection tasks. In addition, we adopt a Tiny Vision Transformer backbone to reduce computational cost, making the framework suitable for real-time deployment on edge devices in railway monitoring systems. We construct a domain-specific dataset collected from real-world freight inspection stations and conduct extensive evaluations. Experimental results show that our method achieves 74.6 APbox and 74.2 APmask on the dataset, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and robustness while maintaining low computational overhead. This work offers a deployable and efficient vision solution for automated freight train inspection, demonstrating the potential of foundation model adaptation in industrial-scale fault diagnosis scenarios. title: A Deep Vision Segmentation Framework for Weld Defect Detection and Structural Integrity Analysis
authors: Celles A.K.M.; Leviste L.R.A.; Lim K.H.W.; Santeco E.S.; Comia L.V.
src: Proceedings of 8th International Conference on Intelligent Sustainable Systems, ICISS 2026
abstract: Ensuring the structural integrity of welded joints is critical in industrial manufacturing, where undetected defects may compromise safety and long-term performance. This study presents a deep vision segmentation framework for automated weld defect detection and analysis using a YOLOv12-based architecture. The proposed approach simultaneously performs object detection and instance segmentation to identify welding lines, cracks, porosity, and spatters from weld surface images. A comprehensive preprocessing and data augmentation pipeline was employed to enhance feature clarity and model robustness, while standardized evaluation metrics were used to assess both bounding box localization and mask-based segmentation performance. Experimental results demonstrate strong overall accuracy, achieving a bounding box mAP50 of 0.818 and a segmentation mAP50 of 0.782, with welding line and crack classes showing the highest reliability due to their distinct structural characteristics. Performance degradation under stricter IoU thresholds highlights the inherent challenges of delineating diffuse and irregular defects such as porosity and spatters, a trend further confirmed through precision-recall analysis and confusion matrix evaluation. Qualitative testing on unseen images validates the model's generalization capability, and a web-based deployment illustrates its practical feasibility for real-time inspection. Overall, the proposed framework offers an effective and scalable solution for automated weld quality assessment, with potential applications in intelligent manufacturing and industrial inspection systems. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Teaching AI-Integrated Engineering Through Project-Based Learning: A Case Study on Deep Learning for Solar PV Fault Detection

abstract: Engineering education faces growing pressure to equip graduates with competencies spanning artificial intelligence (AI), renewable energy systems, and professional engineering practice. title: Research on Weld Seam Extraction Based on Multi-Dimensional Information Fusion
authors: Zhao Y.; Chi Y.
src: 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference, CCDC 2026
abstract: Weld extraction is a key technical challenge in the field of robotic automated welding. Aiming at the problem that cluttered information interferes with the accurate extraction of weld features when depth cameras collect data in complex industrial environments, this paper proposes a weld extraction method based on multi-dimensional information fusion. Firstly, an improved weld region segmentation model, MFT-YOLOv11seg, is proposed. This model introduces the Meta-TSSA module, which enhances the backbone network's ability to locate weld regions through an efficient attention mechanism and linear complexity design. It also introduces the Focal-Modulation module, which improves the model's adaptive ability to complex scenes through a cross-scale feature dynamic interaction mechanism. In addition, an efficient TDAS-Head segmentation head is proposed, which shares the neck network features and uses dynamic convolution and dynamic feature selection for task decomposition and alignment mechanism, reducing the number of parameters while ensuring performance. Based on this, a precise spatial alignment mechanism between 2D instance segmentation masks and 3D depth data is proposed to provide high-quality initial point cloud data for the subsequent refined extraction of welds. Finally, the 3D weld extraction from the initial point cloud data is completed through straight line fitting based on plane intersection. Experimental data show that this method achieves a maximum average error of 1.197 mm, meeting the process requirements of high-precision welding. The MFT-YOLOv11-seg model has significantly improved performance, with increases of 7.4% and 2.12% in mAP 75 and mAP50:95 indicators respectively compared to the baseline, meeting the requirements of high-precision segmentation of weld regions. © 2026 IEEE.

title: YOLO-Bubble: A Lightweight and High-Precision Instance Segmentation Model for Industrial Bubble Detection With BubConv Enhancement
authors: Yang W.; Li J.; Jin J.; Chen H.; He W.; Huang W.
abstract: Rapid and accurate measurement of bubble size is important for industrial visual inspection, because bubbles provide useful morphological cues for process control, material quality assessment, and product state evaluation. Typical scenarios include bubble distribution analysis in porous industrial materials and bubble inspection for Baijiu, a traditional Chinese distilled spirit. Although the imaging media differ, these tasks share common visual challenges, including small targets, low contrast, dense adhesion, irregular contours, and strict requirements for real-time deployment. Existing deep learning models often struggle to balance detection speed and accuracy, making their deployment on edge devices in industrial scenarios challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel, lightweight, and efficient bubble instance segmentation algorithm based on the YOLO11-seg instance segmentation framework, named YOLO-Bubble. First, through feature layer redundancy analysis, a differential channel adjustment strategy is adopted to reduce the model burden. Second, BubConv is designed as a bubble-specific feature enhancement convolution module, where trainable kernels are optimized end-to-end under branch-specific center-response, contrast-enhancement, and angular-difference transformations. Unlike conventional multi-branch convolution modules that mainly increase generic feature diversity, BubConv constrains the weight search space with bubble morphological priors and reparameterizes all branches into a single standard convolution during inference. Finally, a lightweight segmentation head is proposed by reconstructing the feature processing sequence and introducing partial convolution. Experiments are conducted in two representative bubble inspection scenarios: gypsum board bubbles and Baijiu bubbles. Across five independent random seeds, YOLO-Bubble achieves an AP of 61.8±0.4% on the self-built gypsum board bubble dataset, improving YOLO11n-seg by 3.3 percentage points, and an AP of 43.7±0.6% on the Baijiu bubble dataset, improving YOLO11n-seg by 2.3 percentage points. Meanwhile, the parameter count is reduced by 28.4% and GFLOPs by 21.9%. On an edge industrial controller equipped with an Intel Processor N97 CPU, YOLO-Bubble reduces latency from 58.10 ms to 34.16 ms, increases edge-device FPS from 17.21 to 29.27, and lowers peak memory from 615.26 MB to 550.53 MB compared with YOLO11n-seg. These results provide a technical basis for real-time online bubble measurement across industrial production and quality inspection scenarios.  © 2026 The Authors.

title: UVInsDet: A Ground-Based Robotic Inspection Dataset for Insulator Detection and Instance Segmentation in High-Voltage Substations
authors: Khalyasmaa A.I.; Matrenin P.V.; Iumanova I.F.
abstract: Existing publicly available datasets for insulator recognition primarily focus on overhead transmission lines and are commonly acquired using unmanned aerial vehicles. As a result, they often do not reflect the visual complexity of high-voltage substation environments, which are characterized by dense equipment arrangements, structured industrial backgrounds, frequent occlusions, and substantial variation in object scale. To address this gap, we present UVInsDet, a real-world dataset for insulator-string detection and instance segmentation collected during ground-based robotic inspections of an operational 220 kV substation. The dataset comprises 591 visible-spectrum RGB images acquired using a narrow-angle diagnostic inspection camera and contains 1415 manually annotated insulator-string instances represented by pixel-wise segmentation masks. The images cover daytime and nighttime conditions, varying weather scenarios, different viewing angles, and both target-object and negative samples corresponding to realistic inspection workflows. The dataset includes annotations for glass and porcelain insulator strings and provides data in both LabelMe and COCO formats. UVInsDet is intended as a specialized resource for computer vision research in industrial inspection environments. The dataset can support the development and evaluation of object detection and instance segmentation methods, studies of small-object recognition in complex scenes, robustness assessment under varying observation conditions, domain adaptation research, and the development of intelligent monitoring and inspection systems for power infrastructure. title: MMNet: Integration Multi-Attention and Multi-Strategy Network for Feature Recognition
authors: Ma S.; Fang X.; Han L.
src: CMES - Computer Modeling in Engineering and Sciences
abstract: Automated feature recognition (AFR) plays an important role in automated measurement path planning and metrological data processing in the manufacturing industry. Existing AFR methods face critical limitations, such as the loss of geometric-topological fidelity during Computer-aided design (CAD) model conversion and inadequate instance segmentation for dimensional metrology. To address these challenges, we propose an integrated multi-attention and multi-strategy network (MMNet) for feature recognition, which mainly includes the multi-attention geometric and attribute fusion module (MGAM) and the multi-strategy semantic and instance segmentation module (MSIM). Specifically, MGAM employs multi-attention mechanisms to synergize local geometric features with global attributes of the boundary representation (B-rep) to enhance recognition precision. Subsequently, MSIM integrates a graph neural network for face-level semantic segmentation with rule-based instance clustering to achieve robust feature recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods on MFCAD, MFCAD++, and our real-world datasets. Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: An integrated YOLOv11-based framework for wheat spike phenotyping segmentation and grain yield estimation
authors: Solimani F.; Mushtaq N.; Fania F.; Colecchia S.A.; Laidò G.; Pecchioni N.
abstract: Spike count and spatial arrangement are among the strongest determinants of grain yield in wheat, yet reliable spike-level phenotyping under field conditions remains challenging. Field-acquired images are often affected by occlusion, heterogeneous illumination, and dense canopy overlap. In addition to these visual complexities, the effort required to generate large-scale instance-level annotations makes it difficult to build the extensive labeled datasets typically needed for robust segmentation models. This paper addresses both problems. The core methodological contribution is a semi-automated iterative annotation workflow: a YOLOv11x-seg model trained on a small manually annotated set is applied to unlabeled field images, and its predictions, after post-processing to remove duplicated, fragmented, and merged detections, are incorporated back into training. To prevent augmentation from distorting the training distribution, we introduce a distribution-aware augmentation strategy guided by Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), which retains only those augmented samples that remain within an acceptable distance from the original data distribution. Together, these components allowed us to build an effective training set from 3899 high-resolution RGB images (4000 × 3000 pixels) of durum wheat collected at the CREA Research Centre for Cereal and Industrial Crops, with substantially reduced manual annotation effort. On the independent test set(242 images), the final YOLOv11x-seg model (M5 model) achieved a mask-level precision of 86.73%, recall of 83.02%, F1-score of 84.83%, mAP@50 of 89.42%, and mAP@50:95 of 60.51%.Spike masks were used to derive image-based traits including spike count, spike density, canopy coverage, spike area, spatial distribution, and vegetation indices. Their relationships with measured grain yield were explored through statistical analysis and machine-learning-based yield estimation.Both statistical and machine-learning analyses demonstrated that image-derived spike traits provided meaningful information for grain yield estimation, with canopy coverage showing the strongest positive association with yield. Using repeated nested cross-validation with out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, XGBoost achieved the highest yield estimation performance ((Formula presented), RMSE = 106.61 g/plot), supporting the potential of near-image phenotyping for late-stage yield estimation in wheat.These results show that semi-automated iterative annotation can enable practical wheat spike segmentation and image-based phenotyping under realistic open-field conditions. While grain yield estimation should be interpreted within the context of the experimental setting, the proposed framework highlights the value of image-derived spike traits for late-stage phenotyping and yield assessment in breeding experiments rather than for early-season yield forecasting. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V. title: GSSW-YOLO：Real-Time Cable Instance Segmentation for Automated Wiring
authors: Li C.; He W.; Zhang M.; Li C.; Cao R.; Huang J.
abstract: In the context of industrial automated wiring, the instance segmentation of slender and flexible cables remains a significant challenge due to frequent occlusions, complex spatial entanglements, and strict real-time processing requirements. Existing segmentation algorithms typically target sparse or low-density cable scenarios, limiting their applicability in realistic, high-instance-density environments. To address these limitations, we propose GSSW-YOLO, a novel cable instance segmentation framework derived from YOLO11n-seg, with specific adaptations for densely arranged and flexible cable layouts. The architecture builds upon the PP-HGNetV2 backbone, incorporating GhostConv modules to reduce computational overhead and constructing a lightweight GHGNet backbone. In the neck, the standard Conv and C3k2 layers are replaced by GSConv and VoVGSCSP modules from SlimNeck, while the WFU mechanism from WFEN is embedded into the upsampling and feature fusion stages, forming the Slim-WFUNeck. Furthermore, a specialized detection head, Shared Convolutional Separate BN segmentation (SCSBS) Head integrates shared convolution and batch normalization to improve multi-object detection accuracy without increasing model complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method, achieving mAP@0.5 of 90.9%, representing a 4.3% improvement over the conventional YOLO11n-seg baseline. Additionally, the proposed model sustains a real-time inference speed of 85.6 FPS, demonstrating real-time suitability for industrial automation. © 2026, International Association of Engineers. title: Early Detection and Quantitative Assessment of Wind Turbine Blade Surface Defects for Failure Prevention
authors: Meng S.; Gong W.; Xia L.; Niu S.; Zhang L.
src: Journal of Failure Analysis and Prevention
abstract: Cracks, skin delamination, and lightning stroke damage are common failure modes in wind turbine blades. If neglected, they may cause serious structural failures. To enable automated and precise instance segmentation, this paper proposes a “Scale-Channel-Space” synergistic framework, aiming to mitigate geometric mismatch and feature coupling in standard CNNs. A lightweight architecture based on MobileNetV3 is constructed to achieve a favorable trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. To enhance feature preservation under lightweight compression, a bidirectional feature pyramid network (BiFPN) is integrated with efficient channel attention (ECA) for multi-scale feature fusion and channel-wise feature reweighting. Furthermore, deformable convolutions are introduced to construct a topological-aware alignment mechanism, expanding the effective receptive field for irregular shapes. To address limited and imbalanced industrial data, systematic data augmentation and focal loss are adopted. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a bbox AP50 of 91.28% and a mask AP50 of 89.83% on the constructed dataset, outperforming the evaluated baselines. With 13.8 M parameters and 29.7 FPS inference speed, accuracy and efficiency are effectively balanced. Finally, a PyQt5-based visual inspection platform is developed to output pixel-level segmentation results and calculate mask areas in pixels, providing practical support for on-site blade inspection and preliminary damage characterization. © ASM International 2026.

title: From debris to data: benchmarking state-of-the-art computer vision models for intelligent valorization of construction and demolition waste
authors: Malla H.J.; Mohandes S.R.; Hosseini M.R.; Arashpour M.
abstract: Automating construction and demolition waste (CDW) sorting remains difficult because materials vary widely in shape, scale, appearance, and often occur in heavy clutter. Existing datasets fall short of capturing this complexity, which limits the reliability of current computer vision models. This study presents a benchmark dataset of 408 high-resolution CDW images containing nearly 10,000 annotated objects across seven material categories (brick, concrete, glass, metal, paper, plastic, and wood). Images were collected from skip bins, active construction and demolition sites, and municipal solid waste bins to reflect the clutter and disorder typical of primary sorting conditions in material recovery facilities (MRFs). Using this dataset, we evaluate one end-to-end instance segmentation model and two modular pipelines that pair state-of-the-art detectors with a foundation segmentation model, enabling clear diagnosis of model behavior and simple future upgrades. Transformer- and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based detectors show distinct scale-dependent strengths. A key operational insight is also identified. Increasing the confidence threshold from 0.01 to 0.1 in the Transformer-based modular pipeline reduces inference latency by 63.81% with only a 1.42% drop in mean average precision. This positions confidence tuning as a practical mechanism for managing the trade-off between throughput and material purity. Overall, this work introduces a realistic CDW benchmark dataset, establishes modular recognition pipelines, and offers actionable guidance for deploying scalable, high-performance sorting systems in MRFs. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: SCID-Net: Few-shot deep-hole defect instance segmentation via multi-grained feature coupling and instance-aware inference decoupling
authors: Zhao Z.; Kang J.; Xu Y.; Liang J.; Feng L.; Ren Y.; Xue T.; Wu B.
abstract: Accurate instance segmentation of deep-hole inner surface defects is critical for ensuring the structural integrity and functional reliability of high-precision industrial components. However, this task remains highly challenging due to the extreme scarcity of annotated data, along with the irregular morphology, weak texture, and dense, random spatial distribution of defects. Existing instance segmentation methods typically rely on large-scale supervision, which is prohibitively expensive and often infeasible in real-world manufacturing. While few-shot learning offers a promising alternative, current models primarily focus on semantic segmentation and fail to delineate individual defect instances with accurate boundaries and counts. Moreover, they lack adaptive mechanisms to model fine-grained morphological variations of defect regions and are susceptible to foreground–background ambiguity induced by incomplete annotations, resulting in classification bias during inspection. To address these limitations, we propose SCID-Net, a novel few-shot defect instance segmentation framework based on multi-granularity feature coupling and instance-aware inference decoupling. Specifically, we introduce a Multi-Grained Coupling Module (GCM) to facilitate hierarchical bi-directional interaction between support and query features, enriching both class-level prototypes and instance-specific representations. Built upon this, the Instance-Aware Inference Decoupling Module (IAM) decouples dense inference into specialized pathways, and further integrates adaptive spatial modulation and prototype-driven semantic alignment to suppress noise from incomplete annotations. Extensive experiments on a proprietary industrial deep-hole defect dataset demonstrate that SCID-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance under few-shot settings. Moreover, evaluations on NEU-Seg and MS COCO further validate the exceptional generalization capability of SCID-Net, highlighting its versatility in both challenging industrial environments and diverse real-world scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: WormNet: An Automated Deep Learning Platform for Robust and High-Throughput C. elegans Behavior Analysis
authors: Shi Q.; Shi Y.; Li S.; Fu L.; Gu J.; Qiao Y.; Sandall I.; Lim E.G.; Song P.
src: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Caenorhabditis elegans is a model organism widely used in genetics, neuroscience, aging, and toxicology, where quantitative behavior analysis is essential for high-throughput screening and phenotype assessment. Automated worm tracking and analysis software based on traditional image processing has been developed to reduce manual workload, but such methods still degrade markedly under low contrast, lighting drift, and dense multi-worm conditions, limiting real-world scalability and robustness. Based on microscope imaging and deep learning, we develop WormNet, an integrated hardware-software platform for automated C. elegans behavior analysis with enhanced accuracy and throughput. The system combines a temperature-controlled motorized stage, bright-field microscope, and industrial camera, enabling stable acquisition of multi-worm videos under controlled experimental conditions. On the algorithmic side, a multi-scale backbone with a simplified snake convolution (SimSnake Conv) module is used to accurately detect worms, while a multi-scale cross-modal gated fusion (MCGF) module fuses detection features to refine instance masks. A downstream tracking and skeletonization pipeline then automatically calculates morphology and motility parameters, including body length, width, speed, and bending angle. Through experiments on two representative datasets, WormDrop-Micro and WormDish-Real, the system achieves maximum to 1.90% improvement in AP50 and 28.50% improvement in mAP50 over state-of-the-art (SOTA) detectors, and in terms of segmentation accuracy, the Dice coefficient was improved by up to 1.71%, and mIoU by 3.00%. The WormNet pipeline further achieved a processing speed of 20.45 FPS and supported batch analysis of multi-worm videos containing up to approximately 30 worms per field of view. With this performance, WormNet enables robust, fully automated, and high-throughput C. elegans behavior analysis under diverse experimental conditions, making large-scale drug and toxicology screening studies feasible. Note to Practitioners - In the field of worm behavior and drug screening, many laboratories still rely on manual interpretation or semi-automated software to complete multi-worm behavior analysis, which significantly limits throughput, objectivity, and batch-to-batch consistency. This article aims to introduce the functionality and performance of our WormNet automated platform for high-throughput worm behavior analysis. Using this system, researchers can automatically complete processes such as multi-worm video acquisition, worm detection, instance segmentation, trajectory tracking, and quantification of behavioral and morphological parameters in real-world experimental scenarios. We provide a user-friendly graphical interface. Researchers only need to culture worms according to existing procedures and place samples on the platform. By selecting the field of view and analysis parameters through the interface, the system can automatically output structured data such as body length, body width, speed, and bending angle at the single-worm level for subsequent statistical analysis and dose-response assessment. This platform boasts advantages such as high automation, high analytical throughput, and is expected to liberate researchers from tedious frame-by-frame annotation and manual counting, providing a stable and reliable behavioral quantification tool for neurological function research, toxicological evaluation, and drug screening.  © 2004-2012 IEEE.

title: LGG-YOLO-Seg: A Lightweight Real-Time Instance Segmentation Framework for Low-Grade Graphite Ore Sorting
authors: Wang J.; Yu Y.; Yao G.; Qiu Z.; Sun Z.
abstract: Real-time instance segmentation of low-grade graphite ores is essential for intelligent mineral-sorting systems, yet existing methods often struggle to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and lightweight deployment under irregular boundaries, multi-scale targets, and complex illumination conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes LGG-YOLO-Seg, a lightweight and efficient instance segmentation framework based on YOLO11-seg. First, a compact baseline is constructed through depth scaling to reduce redundant computation and model complexity. Then, Linear Deformable Convolution (LDConv) is embedded into the backbone to enhance adaptive feature extraction for irregular ore boundaries. Meanwhile, the feature extraction module is redesigned as C3k2-PKI using multi-kernel and depthwise separable convolutions to improve multi-scale representation capability. In addition, a lightweight Segment-EfficientHead is introduced to reduce computational overhead while maintaining segmentation accuracy. Experiments conducted on a self-constructed graphite ore dataset demonstrate that LGG-YOLO-Seg improves mAP50box and mAP50mask by 0.9% and 0.4%, respectively, compared with YOLO11n-seg while reducing FLOPs, parameters, and model size by 28.8%, 55.6%, and 55.1%, respectively, with an 11.0% increase in inference speed, showing strong potential for real-time industrial sorting and edge deployment. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Automatic optical online inspection system for nibs in electronic carrier tapes and its industrial validation
authors: Zhang M.; Chen S.
abstract: Nibs in electronic carrier tapes are a critical factor leading to device packaging failure. Their online inspection faces challenges such as difficulties in detecting small targets and high rates of missed and false detections. This paper aims to construct a comprehensive automatic optical online inspection system and subject it to thorough industrial validation. The core of the system comprises a self-constructed dataset of nibs, a detection model optimized for small defects based on an instance segmentation framework, and integrated inspection software developed for the production line environment. Field testing results demonstrate that the system achieves a recognition accuracy of 97.26% for nib defects, with a significant reduction in both missed and false detection rates compared to conventional methods. Ultimately, the system has been successfully deployed on an actual production line, delivering an average processing speed of 37 milliseconds per image. Its stable operation fully validates the high precision, high efficiency, and strong robustness of the system, underscoring its considerable value for engineering applications. © 2026 Published under licence by IOP Publishing Ltd.

title: Attention-Enhanced YOLOv8-Seg with WGAN-GP-Based Generative Data Augmentation for High-Precision Surface Defect Detection on Coarsely Ground SiC Wafers
authors: Huang C.-Y.; Shi H.-R.; Xie M.-Y.
abstract: Quality control plays a critical role in modern manufacturing. With the rapid development of electric vehicles, 5G communications, and the semiconductor industry, high-speed and high-precision detection of surface defects on silicon carbide (SiC) wafers has become essential. This study developed an automated inspection framework for identifying surface defects on SiC wafers during the coarse grinding stage. The complex machining textures on wafer surfaces hinder conventional machine vision models, often leading to misjudgment. To address this, deep learning algorithms were applied for defect classification. Because defects are rare and imbalanced across categories, data augmentation was performed using a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP), along with conventional methods. An improved YOLOv8-seg instance segmentation model was then trained and tested on datasets with different augmentation strategies. Experimental results showed that, when trained with WGAN-GP–generated data, YOLOv8-seg achieved mean average precision values of 87.0% (bounding box) and 86.6% (segmentation mask). Compared with the traditional WGAN-GP, the proposed model reduced Fréchet inception distance by 32.2% and multiscale structural similarity index by 29.8%, generating more realistic and diverse defect images. The proposed framework effectively improves defect detection accuracy under limited data conditions and shows strong potential for industrial applications. Copyright © 2026 The Authors.

title: Non-equilibrium crystallization and spatial fingerprints in flash IR-annealed halide perovskite films
authors: Vaccarelli O.; Caldara T.A.; Gisler C.; Hennebert J.; Alonso S.S.
abstract: Metal–halide perovskite solar cells combine high power-conversion efficiencies with solution processability, yet scalable fabrication remains limited by incomplete control over crystallization pathways and the resulting film heterogeneity. Under flash infrared annealing (FIRA), millisecond photonic pulses drive strongly non-equilibrium nucleation and growth, producing spherulitic microstructures whose final geometry stores measurable comparative signatures of the underlying crystallization pathway. Here, we establish a segmentation-based framework that converts bright-field microscopy of FIRA-processed films into quantitative comparative descriptors of grain morphology, video-anchored effective kinetics, and spatial microstructural fingerprints, providing a practical route to analyze crystallization under manufacturing-relevant rapid-processing conditions. Using time-resolved crystallization videos of pristine FAPI and FAPI–TEMPO together with a larger static microscopy dataset of roughly 3000 images from about 100 processed films, we quantify how additive chemistry reorganizes crystallization across both dynamic and end-state image populations. The workflow combines semi-supervised instance segmentation and mask-quality classification with grain-level morphology extraction and video-anchored kinetic reconstruction, with the video data providing the kinetic anchor and the static dataset providing the principal statistical support. From a curated library of more than 420 000 validated spherulites (180 545 for FAPI and 241 619 for FAPI–TEMPO), we derive effective growth-rate distributions, transformed-fraction curves, empirical kinetic descriptors, and spatial signatures based on texture entropy, defect loading, shape regularity, radial profiles, and crowding metrics. We find that TEMPO delays and narrows the dominant crystallization burst, reduces grain-size dispersion (median area reduced by 34%, Δ = 357 µm2, Cliff's δ = 0.62), reduces optically defect-like outer-front heterogeneity, and contracts the accessible kinetic landscape while preserving the overall spherulitic growth motif. Sample-level nonparametric statistics further show that area, perimeter, equivalent radius, and the effective growth rate are all larger in pristine FAPI, whereas the whole-grain texture entropy (hm) is comparable between the two compositions, indicating that the additive redistributes intragrain disorder spatially rather than changing its total amount. These results are consistent with additive-mediated narrowing of the accessible crystallization pathway under rapid annealing. More broadly, the workflow shows that bright-field imaging can serve as a scalable probe of non-equilibrium crystallization in solution-processed semiconductors and provides a transferable route for linking processing, crystallization dynamics, and final microstructure in rapidly solidified thin films. title: Contour-Based Instance Segmentation with the Aid of Pixel-Wise Classification and Topological Regularization
authors: Jo H.; Kim J.
abstract: Contour-based instance segmentation offers several advantages, such as suppressing isolated outlines and enabling efficient inference, by directly producing vectorized polygons that are well suited for precision manufacturing (e.g., semiconductor/PCB inspection) and geospatial applications (e.g., GIS building extraction). However, existing contour-evolution frameworks remain challenged by two practical issues: 1) limited spatial context when refinement relies on features sampled only at sparse vertices, which hinders the accurate recovery of rapidly varying boundaries, and 2) topological instability, where iterative updates frequently yield self-intersecting (non-simple) polygons that are invalid for downstream metrology and geometry processing. To address these limitations, we propose a contour-based framework with two key contributions. First, we introduce a dense-score-guided refinement scheme that augments contour evolution with an auxiliary pixel classification head predicting a dense interior-exterior score map; this grid-level signal is fused with backbone features and used to guide vertex updates, improving boundary localization. Second, we propose an energy-inspired topological loss that introduces explicit, differentiable geometric constraints on total contour length and curvature, effectively reducing self-intersections during training. Extensive experiments on precision manufacturing datasets (PCB bond finger dataset) and remote-sensing benchmarks (WHU building dataset) demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves boundary accuracy and significantly increases the proportion of geometrically valid, simple (i.e., non-self-intersecting) polygons compared with state-of-the-art contour-based instance segmentation methods.  © 2013 IEEE.

title: Multi-Feature Fusion Identification Method and Experimental Research for Fine Sorting of Domestic Waste Plastics; [生活废塑料精细分选的多特征融合识别方法及实验研究]
authors: Jiang F.; Fang H.; Wang M.
abstract: The efficient fine sorting of domestic waste plastics is crucial for enabling high-value recycling, improving the quality of recycled materials, and enhancing overall energy-conversion efficiency. This study addresses a common limitation of single-sensor systems—the difficulty of simultaneously identifying both material type and color, which constrains sorting accuracy. To overcome this limitation, we propose a multi-feature fusion identification method that integrates RGB vision with near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Polypropylene (PP) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) were selected as representative materials for experiments. A data-acquisition platform was built to synchronously capture 640×640-pixel color images and hyperspectral data in the 935.9 – 1 722.5 nm range. Spectral data were preprocessed by dark and white reference correction, Savitzky-Golay filtering, and standard normal variate (SNV) transformation to remove noise. A feature-band selection strategy based on spectral extrema reduced the 204-dimensional spectral data to a key band interval (1 641.4 – 1 687.2 nm). We developed a dual-branch fusion model that combines a Yolact instance-segmentation network (ResNet50-FPN backbone) in the RGB branch to extract color and contour features, with a support vector machine (SVM) in the NIR branch to classify material types using the selected spectral bands. Decision-level fusion was used to integrate the two branches′ outputs. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a precision of 97%, a recall of 97%, and an overall accuracy of 96% when classifying six categories of waste plastics (transparent, white, and colored PP and PET). These results represent an overall improvement of 6 – 7 percentage points across the evaluated metrics compared with an RGB-only baseline (Yolact). The feature-band selection strategy compresses spectral dimensionality by 99.2%, effectively reducing model complexity and the risk of overfitting. The proposed method provides a general and adaptable framework for algorithm development in automated sorting equipment. Validated on real-world production waste samples, the fusion architecture can be extended to identify other domestic waste plastics (e.g., PS, PVC, HDPE), thereby contributing to improved energy efficiency and environmental benefits through precise material and color sorting. We note a limitation: black plastics, which strongly absorb NIR light, were not included in this study. Future work will consider integrating mid-infrared spectroscopy or X-ray sensing for black plastic identification, evaluating lightweight backbone networks for real-time processing, exploring joint optimization of band selection and feature extraction, and investigating adaptive dynamic fusion strategies to enhance robustness in complex scenarios. The framework's adaptability and the demonstrated performance gains underscore its potential for practical industrial deployment in waste management systems. © 2026 CCTEG Hangzhou Research Institute Co., Ltd. title: BeltTear-seg: A lightweight model for belt tear segmentation with multi-scale feature squeeze attention and enhanced classification decision
authors: Yuan L.; Zhou H.; Kong Y.; Liu L.; Li J.
abstract: To address the challenges of small target tear omission and false detections, complex background interference, and strict real-time requirements in belt tear segmentation for industrial production, this study proposes an improved instance segmentation model based on You Only Look Once version 8 nano (YOLOv8n) for segmentation (YOLOv8n-seg), named BeltTear-seg. First, a Multi-scale Feature Squeeze Attention mechanism (MFSA) is introduced to enhance the model’s capability in capturing small target tear regions, effectively reducing the omission rate. Second, an Enhanced Classification Decision (ECD) layer is incorporated into the model head, working in conjunction with Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network(BiFPN) to reduce the false detection rate. Finally, a lightweight designed Cross Stage Partial with 2 convolutions and feature fusion (Light-C2f) is introduced to significantly enhance computational efficiency while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the BeltTear-seg model performs exceptionally well on a custom-built belt tear instance segmentation dataset, which includes 4,050 images (1,800 negative and 2,250 positive samples) of conveyor belt surfaces collected from real industrial sites, achieving a classification accuracy of 95.9%, which represents a 5.8% improvement over the original model YOLOv8n-seg on the custom dataset. Meanwhile the model’s detection time per frame is shortened by 15.1%. When compared with other mainstream instance segmentation models, this model also demonstrates significant advantages. The proposed improvements not only significantly enhance the accuracy of the instance segmentation model but also simultaneously boost segmentation speed, thereby meeting the dual industrial requirements of high precision and real-time detection for belt tear inspection. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.

title: MUSE: Model-based Uncertainty-aware Similarity Estimation for zero-shot 2D Object Detection and Segmentation
authors: Cho S.; Park S.; Oh I.
src: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision, WACV 2026
abstract: In this work, we present MUSE (Model-based Uncertainty-aware Similarity Estimation), a training-free framework for model-based zero-shot 2D object detection and segmentation. First, MUSE incorporates 2D multi-view templates from 3D unseen objects and 2D object proposals from the input query image, respectively. In the embedding stage, we propose a new feature embedding scheme which integrates class and patch embeddings. Specifically, the patch embeddings are normalized using the generalized mean pooling (GeM). In the matching stage, a joint similarity score is introduced, which integrates an absolute score and a relative score. Finally, we update the similarity score using an uncertainty-aware object prior. MUSE achieves state-of-the-art performance on the BOP Challenge 2025, ranking first in the Classic Core, H3, and Industrial tracks - without any additional training or fine-tuning. Therefore, we believe that MUSE is a promising framework for zero-shot 2D object detection and segmentation. © 2026 IEEE.

title: An Approach to Crayfish Weight Estimation Based on Pose Awareness
authors: Ye X.; He M.; Wang J.; Huang L.; Xu J.; Zhang R.; Li B.
abstract: To address the challenges of low accuracy and poor robustness in industrial crayfish weight estimation caused by variable postures, this paper proposes a lightweight method that integrates pose awareness. First, a multi-task perception model, Crayfish-YOLO, is developed based on the YOLOv8s-Seg framework. By reconstructing the backbone with MobileNetV3 and integrating Coordinate Attention (CA), CARAFE upsampling, and the Wise Intersection over Union (Wise-IoU) loss function, the model is significantly compressed while enhancing its ability to output high-fidelity pixel-level masks and pose categories. Second, a pose-adaptive weight estimation strategy is proposed, which leverages perceived pose information to dynamically invoke the optimal regression model from a pre-constructed heterogeneous model library. Using seven core geometric features extracted from the segmentation masks, the system achieves precise weight estimation. Experimental results on a self-built dataset show that Crayfish-YOLO reduces parameters by 75.2% compared to YOLOv8s-Seg, while core segmentation accuracy (mAP50~95 (Seg)) improves by 1.1%. The integrated end-to-end system achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.1 g and a mean coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.92, significantly outperforming comparative algorithms. This research provides an efficient visual perception and estimation solution for the automated grading of crayfish and similar non-rigid aquatic products. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Segmentation and Classification of Welding Beads on Shear Reinforcement With Dual Anchorage Using Deep Learning Models
authors: Mlyahilu J.; Kim J.
abstract: Automated visual inspection in industrial manufacturing requires robust and efficient instance segmentation systems capable of real-time operation without compromising accuracy. This paper presents an enhanced 4-camera framework for welding bead detection and quality assessment, leveraging a novel integration of optimized deep learning architectures and a Green's theorem-based classifier. We conduct a comparative analysis of seven (7) state-of-the-art models for instance segmentation, which are YOLO11, DeepLabV3+, Mask R-CNN, YOLACT++, Cascade R-CNN, SOLOv2, and a Hybrid CNN-Transformer by evaluating their performance on a meticulously annotated dataset acquired under varying illumination and resolution conditions. The modified YOLO11 model is the main contribution of this work, particularly it unifies instance segmentation and classification within a single-stage pipeline for a single class and object, achieving a superior balance between speed and accuracy. Experimental results show that while Cascade R-CNN provides the competitive average precision (mIoU: 0.955 @ 0.5–0.95) and YOLACT++ attaining the best detection metrics (Accuracy: 0.974, Recall: 0.964), the proposed algorithm offers a competitive performance (Accuracy: 0.958, Precision: 0.935, Recall: 0.946) with an extraordinary speed exceeding 32 FPS. The system combines a four-camera system and a mathematical-based quality assessment rule that rules out beads derived from Green's theorem. This study shows that the suggested tool offers a practical, effective, and extremely accurate solution for welding bead segmentation and classification processes in real-time, successfully meeting the crucial need for automated and dependable quality control systems in weld environments or industries. © 2026 The Author(s). title: EAGNet: A graph neural network architecture for machining feature recognition
authors: Wang M.; Yang G.; Du Z.; Wang R.; Peng Y.
src: International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: As a key technology in intelligent manufacturing, machining feature recognition extracts manufacturing semantics from 3D CAD models to link design and manufacturing. Recent deep learning advancements, particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), have gained significant traction due to their suitability for B-Rep’s topological structure, enabling efficient geometric and topological parsing. However, existing GNN-based approaches typically decouple semantic segmentation and instance segmentation into separate tasks, resulting in redundant model architectures and suboptimal computational efficiency. Inspired by the innovative frameworks of EAGIS and AAGNet, we propose EAGNet–a novel GNN architecture based on Edge Adjacency Graph (EAG). This unified framework integrates semantic segmentation and instance segmentation through classification of face adjacency relationships in B-Rep models, effectively reducing model complexity and training overhead. Evaluations on the open-source synthetic dataset MFInstSeg demonstrate that EAGNet achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art learning-based methods while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: SPDF: Structural Prior-Guided Dual-Scale Feature Fusion for Anomaly Detection of Caliper Oil Passages

abstract: To address the industrial detection challenges posed by the slender geometry and low contrast of automotive caliper oil passages as well as the scarcity of defective samples, this paper proposes SPDF, an unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm. The algorithm integrates four core modules: oil passage instance segmentation, dual-scale feature fusion, FastFlow probability density estimation, and structural prior constraint. Trained solely on normal samples, it achieves high-precision anomaly discrimination and pixel-wise defect localization. Experimental results on a self-built X-ray dataset of caliper oil passages demonstrate that SPDF achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.9979, a recall rate of 95.93%, and a false positive rate of 0.41%, outperforming five competitive unsupervised methods. title: YOLO-FR: An enhanced object detector for small object detection in complex scenes
authors: Fan R.; Jiao R.; Nan W.; Dang J.; Wang Z.; Ge X.; Dong B.; Luo X.
src: Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment
abstract: As a key technology, small object detection has shown broad application prospects in the fields of UAV aerial images, remote sensing images, medical diagnosis, intelligent transportation and industrial quality inspection. However, due to the small size of the small object itself, it is susceptible to factors such as low resolution, limited semantic information, and complex background interference, resulting in its detection performance still facing severe challenges. To this end, we propose an improved object detection model YOLO-FR, which aims to improve the detection accuracy and robustness of small objects in complex scenes. Firstly, the C3k2_WT module is designed to expand the receptive field layer by layer and capture the context information by using the cascaded frequency decomposition characteristics of wavelet transform. At the same time, a C3k2_ECA module integrated with Efficient Channel Attention is designed to effectively reduce the number of parameters and enhance the selective response of channel features. Secondly, a small object detection head is introduced to improve the model's support for small object detection. Additionally, the Quad Fusion Downsample downsampling module is proposed to reduce information loss and improve downsampling efficiency. Finally, we compare a variety of emerging Mamba modules to determine the most suitable module for the task of this article, and optimize it on this basis. Our model improves mAP@50:95 by 6.6% and 2.2% on the public benchmark datasets VisDrone2019 and AI-TOD, respectively. At the same time, the parameters of the model are reduced by 36.5%. We also evaluate the segmentation performance of the model on the UAV instance segmentation dataset UAVid, which demonstrates the advancement and applicability of the proposed model in the face of different tasks. title: Physics-informed LSTM-Transformer vision-enhanced system: Real-time axis prediction in tube free-bending manufacturing
authors: Zong Y.; Wang Z.; Zhang S.; Tan J.; Guo X.; Cheng C.; Xiang Y.
abstract: The free-bending technique, distinguished by its exceptional flexibility in axis control, is emerging as a transformative paradigm for manufacturing complex tubular structures, overcoming geometric limitations inherent to conventional tube bending manufacturing processes. However, the high flexibility in multi-axis free-bending systems introduces nonlinear control complexities that critically compromise the tube forming accuracy. Real-time machine vision approaches enable in-process tracking of tubular geometric deviations, providing a fast method for axis prediction. To this end, this paper presents a real-time vision-enhanced prediction system that integrates with an LSTM-Transformer framework. A high-precision visual sensing system is developed to capture tube-end trajectory, integrating 3D-printed markers, depth camera, kinematic decoupling, and instance segmentation for accurate motion tracking and process parameter inversion. Subsequently, a physics-informed hybrid LSTM-Transformer architecture is proposed for dynamic bend axis springback prediction, incorporating trajectory-derived physical constraints and multi-objective optimization for spatio-temporal springback prediction during dynamic forming. Additionally, an online differential geometry mapping method for real-time curvature parameter estimation is introduced, eliminating the need for post-scanning and additional equipment, enabling closed-loop process parameter compensation during bending. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the mean absolute error of axial springback prediction by more than 60% compared to traditional theoretical models, with the mean absolute error for all groups remaining below 12 mm. title: Deep learning-powered system for automated detection and quantification of Vickers indentations
authors: Bertolini F.; Mariani M.; Lecis N.
abstract: Hardness testing is a key procedure in materials science for evaluating mechanical properties and process quality. Traditional Vickers hardness measurement relies on manual identification of indentation diagonals, a process that is slow, subjective, and prone to variability. This work introduces a deep learning-based pipeline for fully automated Vickers hardness measurement, combining instance segmentation via Mask R-CNN with sub-pixel geometric fitting for diagonal extraction. A dataset of 403 micrographs of samples under loads from 10 gf to 2000 gf was assembled and annotated for training and validation. Hyperparameter optimisation was performed using a Taguchi design of experiments, and the final model achieved near-perfect segmentation accuracy (overall AP ≈ 90.5%) on the test set. Measurement accuracy was assessed against manual ground truth, yielding mean relative errors of 1.6-1.9% for the two diagonals, with most cases within 2-3%. These results demonstrate that the proposed system provides robust detection, high metrological precision, and reproducible performance across diverse imaging conditions, paving the way for reliable, high-throughput hardness testing in industrial and research settings. © 2026, Associazione Italiana di Metallurgia. title: Semantic 3D product modelling for automated inspection in remanufacturing processes
authors: Kaiser J.-P.; Koch D.; Stamer F.; Peeters J.; Lanza G.
abstract: Remanufacturing is a key process for enabling a circular economy by restoring used products, often referred to as cores, to a like-new condition. It still heavily relies on manual work. One exemplary manual task is the visual inspection of cores before further processing. This manual effort arises from uncertainties, such as varying product conditions, a broad variety of product variants, and the lack of product information to support automation. To address these challenges and to enable the automation of visual inspection tasks, flexible and adaptive inspection systems are required. These systems must be capable of automatically detecting defects and performing product-specific inspections across a wide range of product variants. Therefore, this work introduces a semantic 3D product modelling method that integrates two-dimensional (images) and three-dimensional (point cloud) data. With the resulting semantic 3D model, the semantic information, such as detected defects and components requiring closer inspection, can be encoded on a geometric product model. This model provides the information basis for an adaptive inspection approach. Using semantic (U-Net) and instance segmentation approaches (Mask-RCNN), the proposed method assigns each surface point of the 3D model to a specific component, thereby creating the semantic 3D product model during the inspection process. The results show that the method presented can achieve semantic 3D modelling both in accuracy and model completeness, encoding component information on the geometric product model. Furthermore, we show that the U-Net architecture used to detect components is also able to detect corrosion as one exemplary defect type, enabling the encoding of various semantic information into the semantic 3D product model. This semantic 3D product model then enables targeted individual inspection of these semantically mapped components and defects on the product model in a later stage of an automated inspection procedure. © The Author(s) 2025.

title: A vision-guided robotic framework for segmentation, separation, and assembly of overlapping puzzle pieces with applications to industrial parts classification
authors: Chen W.-H.; Wu Q.-H.; Lin A.C.
abstract: Overlapping objects remain a significant challenge for vision-guided robotic systems due to severe occlusion, feature ambiguity, and the high cost of manually generating large-scale annotated datasets. Although deep learning has achieved promising performance in object segmentation, existing approaches often focus primarily on object recognition and rarely address the complete workflow from object separation to robotic assembly. To address these limitations, this study proposes a vision-guided robotic framework for the segmentation, separation, and assembly of overlapping puzzle pieces, with extension to industrial parts classification. An automated dataset-generation framework is developed to produce large-scale labeled data without manual intervention. A YOLOv11-based instance segmentation model is employed, together with a two-stage overlap-detection strategy that integrates bounding-box filtering and coverage-rate analysis. Furthermore, a repositioning algorithm is introduced to resolve overlap conditions and ensure valid object separation. For robotic assembly, a hybrid matching method combining SIFT-based feature extraction and polar-coordinate transformation is proposed to determine object position and orientation with high accuracy. The complete pipeline is implemented on a robotic system, enabling fully automated assembly. Unlike conventional methods that address segmentation, matching, and robotic manipulation as separate tasks, the proposed framework integrates automated dataset generation, overlap-aware object separation, feature-based matching, and robotic assembly into a unified perception-to-action pipeline. Experimental results demonstrate high performance in segmentation (mAP = 0.974), matching success rate (95.25%), and assembly success rate (90%) under varying overlap conditions. Additional validation on industrial parts classification confirms the generality and scalability of the proposed framework for real-world industrial applications. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A Vision-Guided Adaptive Robotic System for Fabric Gripping
authors: Sang L.; Liu J.; Fu T.; Song R.
src: 2026 7th International Conference on Mechatronics Technology and Intelligent Manufacturing, ICMTIM 2026
abstract: In garment manufacturing automation, handling flexible fabrics presents several core challenges. These include easy deformation, frequent folding, poor robustness in visual localization, and a lack of real-time gripping point planning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a vision-guided robotic fabric gripping system based on YOLO12 and SAM2.First, the system uses the YOLO12 object detection algorithm to quickly localize the cut fabric parts and extract the Region of Interest (ROI). Second, the SAM2 model performs instance segmentation on the ROI to generate a high-precision binary mask of the target fabric. Then, geometric analysis is applied to determine the optimal gripping points for a flexible gripper. This step ensures fabric flatness during transfer and guarantees a fold-free placement. Finally, the system completes the robotic motion planning and executes the fabric transfer. Compared to methods based on finite element simulation and traditional visual matching, this approach significantly improves real-time performance, robustness, and fold-free gripping results. It provides a feasible technical solution for automated fabric handling in flexible garment production lines. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Design and development of a vision-guided adaptive and adjustable robotic gripper for harvesting apples
authors: Das S.; Paul A.; Machavaram R.
abstract: This study presents the design, fabrication, and laboratory validation of a vision-assisted adaptive robotic gripper for apple harvesting. The proposed end-effector introduces a dual actuation mechanism that integrates a slider–crank and wedge system to achieve a single-degree-of-freedom adaptive grasp, combined with Fin Ray Effect-based flexible TPU fingers for compliant fruit handling. Unlike conventional rigid grippers, the developed mechanism provides a variable trapezoidal workspace (0–158 mm at the fingertip), enabling accommodation of apples with varying diameters while maintaining structural simplicity. The prototype, fabricated using additive manufacturing (TPU fingers and PLA housing), weighs 950 g and demonstrates a load-carrying capacity of 1 kg, exceeding typical apple weights and thereby confirming mechanical robustness. Static structural simulation predicted a maximum contact force of 4.18 N, while experimental validation using a calibrated Force Sensitive Resistor recorded a peak force of 3.91 N, resulting in a relative deviation of 6.56%. These values remain below damage thresholds reported in literature, indicating low risk of fruit bruising under controlled conditions. For vision-based triggering, a YOLOv8s-seg instance segmentation model trained on a laboratory-scale dataset achieved an mAP@0.5 of 0.924, enabling automated actuation through bounding-box detection and ultrasonic distance verification. The gripper demonstrated a complete operational cycle time of 12 s (including a 5 s holding delay) and a peak power consumption of 7.32 W during loading. The results establish the feasibility of integrating soft adaptive mechanics with vision-triggered actuation for gentle and reliable apple handling. While validated in a controlled laboratory environment, the proposed system provides a modular foundation for future integration with robotic manipulators and field-scale orchard deployment. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Real-time Instance Segmentation-based Object Detection and Adaptive Placing Algorithm for Low Cost Bin-picking System; [Manuscript]

abstract: Robots are increasingly utilized in manufacturing and logistics, where bin-picking has become crucial for managing randomly placed objects. To address these challenges, this study presents a cost-effective system that combines a depth camera, YOLO-based instance segmentation, and optimization-based inverse kinematics for real-time object detection and stable manipulation. The results demonstrate that the system maintains stable performance across both picking and placing processes while minimizing reliance on expensive hardware and complex initial setups. By enhancing flexibility and scalability, the proposed approach offers a practical solution for intelligent automation and can serve as a foundation for broader applications in assembly, logistics, and service robotics. title: M2Fusion-SAM: Fine Tuning Based Industrial Image Instance Segmentation Algorithm; [M2Fusion-SAM: 基于微调的工业图像实例分割算法]
authors: WANG L.; YANG Y.; WANG P.; BAI Y.
abstract: Industrial images typically have complex background textures, blurred target edges, metal reflections, and deformation of target components. Existing instance segmentation algorithms commonly suffer from low segmentation accuracy and poor generalization ability when processing industrial images. Based on the segment anything model (SAM) architecture, an instance segmentation algorithm M2Fusion-SAM is proposed. Through a synergistic design that enhances the encoder, generates dynamic prompts, and optimizes the decoder, the model remedies the inherent limitations of SAM in semantic understanding and improves its segmentation accuracy, particularly along complex edges. Firstly, this paper designs an automatic alignment convolutional side adapter that integrates powerful features extracted by SAM into the adapter branch training, achieving comprehensive feature fusion and laying the feature foundation for fine edge segmentation. Secondly, it designs a multi-stage and multi-scale refinement module that can extract fine image position features while preserving semantic information. By continuously accumulating and enhancing, it provides rich fine-grained multi-scale features, further improving the model’s ability to extract detailed features such as edges. Finally, the IAP branch is introduced and combined with a dynamic query decoder, this integrates SAM with semantic information from detection box prompts, leveraging spatial priors to guide the model to focus on target contours, solving the inherent semantic ambiguity of SAM. Through prompt guided segmentation, segmentation accuracy is improved while accelerating the convergence speed of model training. Experiments are conducted on the self-made industrial filling bucket dataset and COCO-mini dataset, and the mAP50-95 of M2Fusion-SAM achieves 97% and 48.3%, respectively, which are 14% and 1% higher than SAM, respectively. When using the ViT-H backbone, the model requires only 4.21×107 trainable parameters, which account for 5.5% of the total parameters. With a small number of trainable parameters, the accuracy of industrial image instance segmentation can be significantly improved, providing reliable technical support for industrial filling processes. © (2026), (Journal of Computer Engineering and Applications Beijing Co.). title: MBCF-YOLO: ENABLING AUTOMATED DEFECT DETECTION AND AREA QUANTIFICATION IN EXPLOSIVE COLUMNS WITH AN ADAPTED YOLO FRAMEWORK
authors: JINGt, L; Xiao, XP; Llt, Z; XIONGt, W; JIANGt, T
abstract: Explosive columns are solid energetic charges used in munitions and industrial blasting that may contain internal holes of various shapes and sizes. In X-ray computed tomography (XCT) images, these internal defects can compromise product quality and safety. However, accurate hole identification remains challenging, and unreliable area estimation further limits quantitative inspection. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multiscale bidirectional context fusion model (MBCF-YOLO), based on YOL0v11, for hole defect instance segmentation in explosive columns. The proposed model enhances multiscale representation and feature fusion by introducing a context fusion block (CFB-C3K2), a multiscale bidirectional fusion module (MSBF-SPPF), and a CARAFE-based upsampling strategy. The model directly outputs instance masks for each hole, while area quantification is performed as a separate post-processing step by applying the Shoelace theorem to the extracted hole contours.

title: PrimitiveGroup: A Fast Primitive Segmentation Framework on Industrial Point Clouds
authors: Huang, AY; Wang, ZT; Li, ZK; Wei, MQ; Wang, J
abstract: Efficiency is crucial for primitive segmentation in industrial applications. Previous state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods suffer from low efficiency due to reliance on time-consuming feature clustering. To circumvent the need for slowly grouping points in a high-dimensional space, we propose a fast framework named PrimitiveGroup (PG), which makes full use of spatial relations and various feature consistency to group points efficiently in the 3-D space. Moreover, to improve the accuracy of point grouping in the 3-D space, we also introduce an adaptive long-range offset prediction module which expands the neighborhood perception range and adaptively focuses on those neighborhoods exhibiting higher semantic and instance correlation. A hybrid consistency aggregation that considers not only spatial distance and semantic constraints but also other geometric consistency of each point is proposed to decompose mixed points belonging to primitives with overlapping or adjacent centroids. Experimental results on the ABCParts and the ANSI datasets show that PG not only achieves competitive performance compared to recent SOTA methods but also operates as the fastest deep learning method in primitive segmentation, 22 times faster than the existing fastest method. Meanwhile, PG achieves promising robustness on noisy point clouds and industrial real scans.
